Anthropic.title: Anthropic expands Claude into an AI office suite.
Anthropic.description: Anthropic expands Claude into an AI office suite. ... On November 10th, Anthropic announced the launch of Claude Sheets, Claude Whiteboards, and Claude Meetings, and officially put Claude Data into operation. ... Another giant wants to 'destroy' Microsoft Office.Anthropic
Anthropic.content:
# Anthropic expands Claude into an AI office suite.

(GLO) - Anthropic has just added a series of new features to Claude, including spreadsheet creation, online meeting support, and idea organization, aiming to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) into many office tasks.

On November 10th, Anthropic announced the launch of Claude Sheets, Claude Whiteboards, and Claude Meetings, and officially put Claude Data into operation.

According to Bloomberg, the new products mark Claude's shift from a tool used by many programmers to a platform serving a broader range of professional and office activities.

Claude Sheets allows users to create spreadsheets from scratch using plain language, adding formulas, multiple worksheets, formatting, and selection lists. The AI can directly edit individual cells, recording changes for user review.

Spreadsheets can be shared for collaboration and exported to Excel or CSV. However, Anthropic states that the tool currently only meets basic needs and is not yet suitable for complex financial models.

You may also like

Another giant wants to 'destroy' Microsoft Office.Anthropic is expanding Claude into an AI-integrated office suite, with capabilities for creating spreadsheets, organizing meetings, and processing data, aiming to compete with Microsoft and Google.

Claude is venturing into the legal field; what careers is AI aiming for?Claude adds tools for contract review, citation checking, and legal regulation tracking, expanding the range of tasks AI can handle.

Anthropic launches data table and animation creation tool on Claude.VTV.vn - Anthropic has launched a tool for creating visual data tables, analyzing data using natural language, and designing animations on the Claude platform, helping to improve work efficiency.

Claude Meetings is designed for participating in online meetings. The tool tracks conversation content, answers questions in the chat window, and creates plans, schedules, and to-do lists as the meeting progresses.

Currently, this feature is being tested with Team and Enterprise customers on Google Meet, before expanding to other platforms.

Meanwhile, Claude Whiteboards provides a shared work board, helping teams translate ideas and discussion points into visual plans with deadlines, responsible individuals, and specific tasks.

Users can continue collaborating directly or convert the results into documents or presentations.

Additionally, Anthropic renamed Claude Dashboards to Claude Data and officially launched the tool.

The product connects to enterprise data systems, allowing users to ask questions, create charts, dashboards, and interpret data.

You may also like

Additionally, Claude expands connectivity with applications such as Adobe, Atlassian, and HubSpot, allowing users to open and interact with these tools directly within the AI work environment.

According to TechCrunch , Anthropic's move comes as OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google are also accelerating the development of AI tools for office work. Microsoft integrated Copilot into Microsoft 365, while Google introduced Gemini into Workspace.

Anthropic.title: Customer support agent
Anthropic.description: Claude actually works best with the bulk of its prompt content written inside the first ... Now that you have your static content, add at least 4–5 sample “good” interactions to guide Claude’s responses. ... Claude is capable of taking actions and retrieving information dynamically using client-side tool use functionality.
Anthropic.content:
# Customer support agent

## Prerequisites

To follow this guide, you need:

- A Claude API key (set as theANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable)
- Python 3.10 or later

Install the required packages:
pip install anthropic streamlit python-dotenv

## Before building with Claude

### Decide whether to use Claude for support chat

Here are some key indicators that you should employ an LLM such as Claude to automate portions of your customer support process:

### High volume of repetitive queries
Claude excels at handling a large number of similar questions efficiently, freeing up human agents for more complex issues.

### Need for quick information synthesis
Claude can quickly retrieve, process, and combine information from vast knowledge bases, whereas human agents might need time to research or consult multiple sources.

### 24/7 availability requirement
Claude can provide support at all hours without fatigue, whereas staffing human agents for continuous coverage can be costly and challenging.

### Rapid scaling during peak periods
Claude can handle sudden increases in query volume without the need for hiring and training additional staff.

### Consistent brand voice
You can instruct Claude to consistently represent your brand’s tone and values, whereas human agents might vary in their communication styles.

Some considerations for choosing Claude over other LLMs:

- You prioritize natural, nuanced conversation: Claude’s sophisticated language understanding allows for more natural, context-aware conversations that feel more human-like than chats with other LLMs.
- You often receive complex and open-ended queries: Claude can handle a wide range of topics and inquiries without generating scripted responses or requiring extensive programming of permutations of user utterances.
- You need scalable multilingual support: Claude’s multilingual capabilities allow it to engage in conversations in over 200 languages without the need for separate chatbots or extensive translation processes for each supported language.

### Define your ideal chat interaction

Outline an ideal customer interaction to define how and when you expect the customer to interact with Claude. This outline will help to determine the technical requirements of your solution.

Here is an example chat interaction for car insurance customer support:

Customer: Initiates support chat experience

- Claude: Warmly greets customer and initiates conversation

Customer: Asks about insurance for their new electric car

- Claude: Provides relevant information about electric vehicle coverage

Customer: Asks questions related to unique needs for electric vehicle insurance

- Claude: Responds with accurate and informative answers and provides links to the sources

Customer: Asks off-topic questions unrelated to insurance or cars

- Claude: Clarifies it does not discuss unrelated topics and steers the user back to car insurance

Customer: Expresses interest in an insurance quote

- Claude: Asks a set of questions to determine the appropriate quote, adapting to their responses
- Claude: Sends a request to use the quote generation API tool along with necessary information collected from the user
- Claude: Receives the response information from the API tool use, synthesizes the information into a natural response, and presents the provided quote to the user

Customer: Asks follow-up questions

- Claude: Answers follow-up questions as needed
- Claude: Guides the customer to the next steps in the insurance process and closes out the conversation

In the real example that you write for your own use case, you might find it useful to write the actual words in this interaction so that you can also get a sense of the ideal tone, response length, and level of detail you want Claude to have.

### Break the interaction into unique tasks

Customer support chat is a collection of multiple different tasks, from question answering to information retrieval to taking action on requests, wrapped up in a single customer interaction. Before you start building, break down your ideal customer interaction into every task you want Claude to be able to perform. This ensures you can prompt and evaluate Claude for every task, and gives you a good sense of the range of interactions you need to account for when writing test cases.

Customers sometimes find it helpful to visualize this as an interaction flowchart of possible conversation inflection points depending on user requests.

Here are the key tasks associated with the example insurance interaction:

Greeting and general guidance

- Warmly greet the customer and initiate conversation
- Provide general information about the company and interaction

Product information

Provide information about electric vehicle coverage This will require that Claude have the necessary information in its context, and might imply that a

is necessary.

Answer questions related to unique electric vehicle insurance needs

Answer follow-up questions about the quote or insurance details

Offer links to sources when appropriate

Conversation management

- Stay on topic (car insurance)
- Redirect off-topic questions back to relevant subjects

Quote generation

- Ask appropriate questions to determine quote eligibility
- Adapt questions based on customer responses
- Submit collected information to quote generation API
- Present the provided quote to the customer

### Establish success criteria

Work with your support team to define success criteria and write detailed evaluations with measurable benchmarks and goals.

Here are criteria and benchmarks that can be used to evaluate how successfully Claude performs the defined tasks:

### Query comprehension accuracy
This metric evaluates how accurately Claude interprets customer inquiries across various topics. Measure this by reviewing a sample of conversations and assessing whether Claude has the correct interpretation of customer intent, critical next steps, what successful resolution looks like, and more. Aim for a comprehension accuracy of 95 percent or higher.

### Response relevance
This assesses how well Claude’s response addresses the customer’s specific question or issue. Evaluate a set of conversations and rate the relevance of each response (using LLM-based grading for scale). Target a relevance score of 90 percent or above.

### Response accuracy
Assess the correctness of general company and product information provided to the user, based on the information provided to Claude in context. Target 100 percent accuracy in this introductory information.

### Citation provision relevance
Track the frequency and relevance of links or sources offered. Target providing relevant sources in 80 percent of interactions where additional information could be beneficial.

### Topic adherence
Measure how well Claude stays on topic, such as the topic of car insurance in the example implementation. Aim for 95 percent of responses to be directly related to car insurance or the customer’s specific query.

### Content generation effectiveness
Measure how successful Claude is at determining when to generate informational content and how relevant that content is. For example, in this implementation, you would be determining how well Claude identifies when to generate a quote and how accurate that quote is. Target 100 percent accuracy, as this is vital information for a successful customer interaction.

### Escalation efficiency
This measures Claude’s ability to recognize when a query needs human intervention and escalate appropriately. Track the percentage of correctly escalated conversations versus those that should have been escalated but weren’t. Aim for an escalation accuracy of 95 percent or higher.

Here are criteria and benchmarks that can be used to evaluate the business impact of employing Claude for support:

### Sentiment maintenance
This assesses Claude’s ability to maintain or improve customer sentiment throughout the conversation. Use sentiment analysis tools to measure sentiment at the beginning and end of each conversation. Aim for maintained or improved sentiment in 90 percent of interactions.

### Deflection rate
The percentage of customer inquiries successfully handled by the chatbot without human intervention. Typically aim for a 70–80 percent deflection rate, depending on the complexity of inquiries.

### Customer satisfaction score
A measure of how satisfied customers are with their chatbot interaction. Usually done through post-interaction surveys. Aim for a CSAT score of 4 out of 5 or higher.

### Average handle time
The average time it takes for the chatbot to resolve an inquiry. This varies widely based on the complexity of issues, but generally, aim for a lower AHT compared to human agents.

## How to implement Claude as a customer service agent

### Choose the right Claude model

The choice of model depends on the trade-offs among cost, accuracy, and response time.

For customer support chat, Claude Opus 5.5 is well suited to balance intelligence, latency, and cost, including the most complex support scenarios that require deep reasoning across long, multistep conversations. However, for instances where you have a conversation flow with multiple prompts including RAG, tool use, or long-context prompts, Claude Haiku 5.5 might be more suitable to optimize for latency. Effort is its main control for speed:low is the fastest level, suited to chat and short tool tasks.

### Build a strong prompt

Using Claude for customer support requires Claude having enough direction and context to respond appropriately, while having enough flexibility to handle a wide range of customer inquiries.

Start by writing the elements of a strong prompt, beginning with a system prompt. Create a file calledconfig.py and add each of the following blocks to it:
IDENTITY = """You are Eva, a friendly and knowledgeable AI assistant for Acme Insurance
Company. Your role is to warmly welcome customers and provide information on
Acme's

[Content truncated]

Anthropic.title: Glossary
Anthropic.description: The Claude API does not currently offer fine-tuning, but ask your Anthropic contact if you are interested in exploring this option. ... Claude, an AI assistant for life and work built by Anthropic, is based on a large language model that has been fine-tuned and trained using RLHF.
Anthropic.content:
# Glossary

## Context window

The “context window” refers to the amount of text a language model can look back on and reference when generating new text. This is different from the large corpus of data the language model was trained on, and instead represents a “working memory” for the model. A larger context window allows the model to process and respond to more complex and lengthy prompts, whereas a smaller context window might limit the model’s ability to handle longer prompts or maintain coherence over extended conversations.

See the guide to understanding context windows to learn more.

## Fine-tuning

Fine-tuning is the process of further training a pretrained language model using additional data. This causes the model to start representing and mimicking the patterns and characteristics of the fine-tuning dataset. Claude is not a bare language model; it has already been fine-tuned to be a helpful assistant. The Claude API does not currently offer fine-tuning, but ask your Anthropic contact if you are interested in exploring this option. Fine-tuning can be useful for adapting a language model to a specific domain, task, or writing style, but it requires careful consideration of the fine-tuning data and the potential impact on the model’s performance and biases.

## HHH

HHH (helpful, honest, harmless) is a research framework that informs how Claude is trained to be beneficial to society. It is distinct from the Claude product tagline, “AI assistant for life and work.”

- A helpful AI will attempt to perform the task or answer the question posed to the best of its abilities, providing relevant and useful information.
- An honest AI will give accurate information, and not hallucinate or confabulate. It will acknowledge its limitations and uncertainties when appropriate.
- A harmless AI will not be offensive or discriminatory, and when asked to aid in a dangerous or unethical act, the AI should politely refuse and explain why it cannot comply.

## Latency

Latency, in the context of generative AI and large language models, refers to the time it takes for the model to respond to a given prompt. It is the delay between submitting a prompt and receiving the generated output. Lower latency indicates faster response times, which is crucial for real-time applications, chatbots, and interactive experiences. Factors that can affect latency include model size, hardware capabilities, network conditions, and the complexity of the prompt and the generated response.

## LLM

Large language models (LLMs) are AI language models with many parameters that are capable of performing a variety of surprisingly useful tasks. These models are trained on vast amounts of text data and can generate human-like text, answer questions, summarize information, and more. Claude, an AI assistant for life and work built by Anthropic, is based on a large language model that has been fine-tuned and trained using RLHF.

## MCP (Model Context Protocol)

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that standardizes how applications provide context to LLMs. Like a USB-C port for AI applications, MCP provides a unified way to connect AI models to different data sources and tools. MCP allows AI systems to maintain consistent context across interactions and access external resources in a standardized manner. See the MCP documentation to learn more.

## MCP connector

The MCP connector is a feature that allows API users to connect to MCP servers directly from the Messages API without building an MCP client. This allows seamless integration with MCP-compatible tools and services through the Claude API. The MCP connector supports features such as tool calling and is available in beta. See the MCP connector documentation to learn more.

## Pretraining

Pretraining is the initial process of training language models on a large unlabeled corpus of text. In Claude’s case, autoregressive language models (such as Claude’s underlying model) are pretrained to predict the next word, given the previous context of text in the document. These pretrained models are not inherently good at answering questions or following instructions, and often require deep skill in prompt engineering to elicit the behaviors you want. Fine-tuning and RLHF are used to refine these pretrained models, making them more useful for a wide range of tasks.

## RAG (retrieval augmented generation)

Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that combines information retrieval with language model generation to improve the accuracy and relevance of the generated text, and to better ground the model’s response in evidence. In RAG, a language model is augmented with an external knowledge base or a set of documents that is passed into the context window. The data is retrieved at runtime when a query is sent to the model, although the model itself does not necessarily retrieve the data (but can with tool use and a retrieval function). When generating text, relevant information first must be retrieved from the knowledge base based on the input prompt, and then passed to the model along with the original query. The model uses this information to guide the output it generates. This allows the model to access and use information beyond its training data, reducing the reliance on memorization and improving the factual accuracy of the generated text. RAG can be particularly useful for tasks that require up-to-date information, domain-specific knowledge, or explicit citation of sources. However, the effectiveness of RAG depends on the quality and relevance of the external knowledge base and the knowledge that is retrieved at runtime.

## RLHF

Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is a technique used to train a pretrained language model to behave in ways that are consistent with human preferences. This can include helping the model follow instructions more effectively or act more like a chatbot. Human feedback consists of ranking a set of two or more example texts, and the reinforcement learning process encourages the model to prefer outputs that are similar to the higher-ranked ones. Claude has been trained using RLHF to be a more helpful assistant. For more details, you can read Anthropic’s paper on RLHF.

## Temperature

Temperature is a parameter that controls the randomness of a model’s predictions during text generation. Higher temperatures lead to more creative and diverse outputs, allowing for multiple variations in phrasing and, in the case of fiction, variation in answers as well. Lower temperatures result in more conservative and deterministic outputs that stick to the most probable phrasing and answers. Adjusting the temperature allows users to encourage a language model to explore rare, uncommon, or surprising word choices and sequences, rather than only selecting the most likely predictions.

Users might encounter non-determinism in APIs. Even with temperature set to 0, the results will not be fully deterministic, and identical inputs might produce different outputs across API calls. This applies both to Anthropic’s first-party inference service and to inference through third-party cloud providers.

## TTFT (time to first token)

Time to first token (TTFT) is a performance metric that measures the time it takes for a language model to generate the first token of its output after receiving a prompt. It is an important indicator of the model’s responsiveness and is particularly relevant for interactive applications, chatbots, and real-time systems where users expect quick initial feedback. A lower TTFT indicates that the model can start generating a response faster, providing a more seamless and engaging user experience. Factors that can influence TTFT include model size, hardware capabilities, network conditions, and the complexity of the prompt.

## Tokens

Tokens are the smallest individual units of a language model, and can correspond to words, subwords, characters, or even bytes (in the case of Unicode). For Claude, the number of characters a token represents depends on the model and the language. Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview use a newer tokenizer that produces approximately 30 percent more tokens for the same text than earlier models, on which a token represents approximately 3.5 English characters. To get exact counts, use token counting with the model you plan to use. Tokens are typically hidden when interacting with language models at the “text” level but become relevant when examining the exact inputs and outputs of a language model. When Claude is provided with text to evaluate, the text (consisting of a series of characters) is encoded into a series of tokens for the model to process. Larger tokens improve data efficiency during inference and pretraining (and are used when possible), whereas smaller tokens allow a model to handle uncommon or never-before-seen words. The choice of tokenization method can impact the model’s performance, vocabulary size, and ability to handle out-of-vocabulary words.

人工智能公司Anthropic1推出ClaudeFable5.2及Claude Mythos5.2，稱新版本在複雜軟件工程、長時間任務及多智能體協作方面有所提升，輸出速度最高較5.1版增加30%，標準API收費降低20%。Fable向一般用戶提供，Mythos則主要開放予通過驗證的網絡安全及生命科學機構。

Anthropic推出Fable5.2及Mythos5.2，標準API收費下調。（網絡圖片）

據Anthropic公佈，新模型適用於開放式技術工作，可處理以往需要反覆調整的工程任務，包括建立三維場景、根據視覺參考重建互動體驗，以及協調大量智能體共同工作。公司把這類能力定位於較長時間、範圍較大的專案，同時表示日常編程和知識工作仍可先使用Opus 5.5，再按任務難度選擇其他模型。

兩款5.2模型的標準價格均為每100萬輸入Token收費8美元，輸出Token收費40美元，較前代降低20%。API支援100萬Token上下文，最大輸出為12.8萬Token。上下文長度是單次任務可處理的資訊範圍，與實際回覆長度並不相同，最終費用仍取決於輸入、輸出及所選服務模式。

公 司 另 提 供 可 選 快 速 模 式， 稱Token生成速度最高可增加至2.5倍，收 費 為 每100萬 輸 入Token16美 元、輸出80美元。快速模式價格高於標準模式，用戶須在速度與成本之間選擇。一般5.2版本較前代最高快30%的說法，與快速模式額外提速屬不同比較，不能合併視作所有工作都有相同增幅。

Fable 5.2與Mythos 5.2採用相同底層能力，但防護及使用資格不同。Fable維持針對敏感網絡安全和生物工作設下的限制；Mythos則透過驗證計劃供合資格機構使用。網絡安全人員可申請專門驗證，生命科學研究者亦可經相應計劃提出使用要求，並非一般帳戶均可直接切換。

在公司內部的漏洞重新發現測試中，Mythos 5.2較Opus 5.5找到的漏洞多10.2%，較Mythos 5.1多14.4%。該輪測試涵蓋1,829項已公開漏洞，衡量模型能否在修補前的程式碼版本自行找到問題。這類結果屬指定資料與設定下的表現，公司亦提醒應參閱系統卡中的方法及限制。

安全評估方面，Anthropic表示，模型接受外部機構測試，並針對誤導用戶、虛報任務完成及未披露失誤等行為進行審核。在刻意設有弱點、部分任務需要越出沙盒才能完成的測試中，Mythos 5.2有3.1%情境使用沙盒外的憑證或檔案，低於5及5.1版本，但風險並未完全消失。

服務安排亦包含持續監察。Anthropic表示，部分複雜濫用須從多次請求的模式識別，一般客戶需保留30天資料供安全監測；企業客戶可申請在自身基礎設施內執行監察的方案，以配合零資料保留要求。相關安排影響敏感工作資料的部署方式，企業需按適用方案啟用服務。

Fable 5.2已透過Claude平台及亞馬遜、谷歌、微軟相關雲端服務提供。公司亦向部分付費方案提供限期額外用量，具體額度依訂閱及席位而異。此次更新與Anthropic推進上市同時進行，對外公佈的速度、測試分數與價格分別對應不同設定，開發者可依公開文件選擇標準或快速模式。

- 【内容简介】
- ChatGPT是由OpenAI公司研发的人工智能聊天机器人，它可以进行自然语言文本的理解和生成。ChatGPT的出现让计算机能够更加自然地与人类进行对话，这标志着人工智能技术在自然语言处理领域取得了革命性的突破，人机交互从此迈入了一个新的时代。
本书将带领读者深入了解ChatGPT，介绍ChatGPT的相关概念、技术原理和实际应用，并探讨人工智能相关技术与产业的发展前景。全书共8章，可划分为3个部分。
第1部分为第1章，以“ChatGPT是什么”为主题。先简单介绍了聊天机器人的概念，然后介绍ChatGPT的核心技术和发明者，接着探讨了ChatGPT成为史上增长最快的消费级应用背后的原因，最后就大众所关心的一些问题做了回答。
第2部分为第2～5章，以“ChatGPT怎么用”为主题。第2章介绍了ChatGPT及其同公司的其他应用型产品（DALL·E2和OpenAIAPI）的基本使用方法。第3章介绍了一些能让ChatGPT的功能更完善的插件。第4、5章通过ChatGPT的一些实际应用案例，展示ChatGPT在各种领域的应用场景和未来发展方向。
第3部分为第6～8章，以“ChatGPT能带来什么”为主题。第6、7章介绍了AIGC（人工智能生成内容）的产业生态及当前比较知名的一些AIGC工具。第8章初步探讨了AIGC可能会在道德、隐私和安全等方面引发的问题。
本书旨在为对ChatGPT感兴趣的读者提供一份较为全面且通俗易懂的资源，帮助他们更好地理解人工智能技术的意义和影响。希望本书能为读者带来关于人工智能技术的新思考，激励更多人投身于人工智能技术的研究和应用，为人工智能技术的发展做出更大的贡献。
- 【目录】

本书将带领读者深入了解ChatGPT, 介绍ChatGPT的相关概念、技术原理和实际应用, 并探讨人工智能相关技术与产业的发展前景。全书共8章, 可划分为3个部分。
主编推荐
2022年12月OpenAI公司的ChatGPT面市了，因为工作原因在2023年1月的时候我进行了一些试用，2月2日我在北京和一些同行交流如何提高工作效率的时候，我谈起起了ChatGPT，但是那时因为很多人都没有使用过ChatGPT所以对它并没有强烈的感觉。在2月6日我离开了北京，当我还在高铁上的时候，就有同事给我打电话说，现在的微信朋友圈全部是ChatGPT。接着的一周ChatGPT的大“火”都是大家知道的了，基本上我关注的公众号都会围绕ChatGPT发布各种帖子和信息。

在我和我的团队看过网上很多关于ChatGPT的介绍和评论，发现网上充满了各种声音与观点。

有些人说“ChatGPT就是一个聊天工具，没啥价值”

有些人说“ChatGPT会取代教师、律师……”

有些人说“ChatGPT回复的内容都是一本正经的胡说八道”

……

这些观点中有一些是非常的客观，但是也有很多是片面的夸大或者误解。同时作为一个文字工作者，我突然想是不是借助ChatGPT来写一本ChatGPT的书，把它应用到一个实际的工作场景中去，从而看看它到底是“骡子”还是“马”，通过这样实际的应用也能发现更多“惊喜”和“无奈”，得到团队成员的支持后，我们就很快投入了这本书的创作中。

当这本书写完的时候，我们团队复盘了这次借助ChatGPT进行创作的过程，我们有以下几个感悟：
ChatGPT确实是一个很好的工具，能提高我们的工作效率。特别是对于一些传统的知识点生产的信息比较饱满和准确。 ChatGPT在创新思维、逻辑思维上还完全不能满足很多用户的需求。在后面书中我们也提到了，它毕竟是基于语料训练出来的一个模型。 掌握和ChatGPT对话的技巧，有助用户获取更准确的知识。 最终这本书的形成还是依靠了我们团队大量的脑力劳动和人工投入。
还有一些我们无法表达的感悟，我们就只能在书中通过一些案例展示给大家。

这本书有不少务虚的地方，主要是为大家展示什么很多关于ChatGPT的概念和前景；也有不少务实的地方，给大家讲解了如何通过ChatGPT提高使用Excel、翻译和编写程序的效率。

本书旨在为对ChatGPT感兴趣的读者提供一份较为全面且通俗易懂的资源，帮助他们更好地理解人工智能技术的意义和影响。希望本书能为读者带来关于人工智能技术的新思考，激励更多人投身于人工智能技术的研究和应用，为人工智能技术的发展做出更大的贡献。

本书有不少内容由ChatGPT在我们的提示下自动生成，其内容我们也尽力去求证、勘误和修改，但是因为作者水平有限，难免出现有不足之处，恳请广大读者批评指正。读者也可以扫描我们封面前勒口上“颉腾文化”的二维码，发送关键词“AI”，我们将回复信息中推送一些非常有价值的文章、资源和源代码供大家使用。

AI Changed More in 4 Years Than You Remember
The Neuron: AI Explained
Play
Corey and Grant walk backward through roughly four years of modern generative AI, starting with late-2026 frontier models and agents and tracing the path back to ChatGPT’s November 2022 launch and the 2017 Transformer paper. The episode focuses on what changed at each stage: reasoning, tools, multimodality, long context, agents, open-source competition, and the shift from chatbots toward long-running computer work. They also revisit their own first encounters with ChatGPT, debate open access versus AI safety, and close with long-term predictions about robotics, machine labor, scientific progress, and who should have access to increasingly capable systems. OpenAI.title: State of LLMs on the Application Layer

OpenAI.content:
# State of LLMs on the Application Layer
import { BlogHeader } from "@/components/blog/BlogHeader";

<BlogHeader title="State of LLMs on the Application Layer" description="We have analyzed model adoption of 20.000+ organizations building LLM applications and agents in the last 12 months. Here is what we found." authors={["felixkrauth"]} date="October 13, 2025" />

## About Langfuse

Langfuse is the leading open source LLM observability platform powering safe and scalable LLM applications for 10s of thousands of organizations. The data on Langfuse Cloud tells a story of a rapidly growing market and allows us to get a unique view on the state of the LLM application layer.

We power global enterprises like Khan Academy, SumUp and Merck as well as AI-native startups like Magic Patterns, Circleback and Juicebox to build safe and scalable LLM applications and agents.

## About this Report

The core of what we do is helping developers to ship LLM applications and agents faster and more reliably. Our dataset gives a unique view on how models are adopted on the application layer instead of consumers that use those models via apps like Claude, Gemini or ChatGPT.

- The data comes from over 20.000 organizations on Langfuse Cloud
- Billions of LLM traces and observations (see data model) on Langfuse Cloud (no self-hosted data included)
- 59 unique models tracked across major providers, longtail of models is not included and grouped into "Other"
- Time Period: 12 months (Oct 2024 - Sep 2025)

## Status Quo in September 2025

Here is where the market stands in September 2025: OpenAI is still the dominant player (55.3%), followed by Google (13.1%) and Anthropic (7.3%). The longtail of models is not included and grouped into "Other" (24.3%).

## Change over the last 12 months

The past 12 months show clear changes in the market.

Provider | Sep 2025 | Oct 2024 | Change 
---|---|---|---
OpenAI | 55.3% | 82.7% | -27.4 pts 
Other | 24.3% | 10.0% | +14.3 pts 
13.1% | 0.5% | +12.6 pts 
Anthropic | 7.3% | 6.8% | +0.5 pts 

## Key Insights

- OpenAI is yielding market share (down -27.4 points) while Google, Anthropic and "Other" model providers grow.
- Google's Rise: Google went from 0.5% → 13.1% (26x) share in just 12 months.
- Anthropic is relatively stable at 7.3%
- "Other" models rising strongly signals that the LLM market is fragmenting beyond the "Big Three," with organizations adopting specialized models, open-source alternatives, and regional providers.

## Market Share by Model

Let's take a look at market shares on model level.

What we see

- The market is operating on a ~6 month effective model lifecycle – Several October 2024 top-20 models effectively disappeared
- Application builders are heavily relying on small efficient models (OpenAI nano or mini: Gemini Flash; Anthropic’s Opus model not relevant)
- The story isn't "OpenAI vs everyone else"—it's fragmentation vs. consolidation. While the Big Three (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic) consolidate around 75% of tracked share, the "Other" 25% represents hundreds of specialized models serving specific use cases, geographies, or price points.

Key Takeaways:

- Organizations aren't building on stable platforms; they're building on a constantly shifting foundation. This creates both opportunity (rapid innovation) and risk (technical debt accumulates fast).
- Staying flexible and being ready to swap out models will pay off when building applications and underlying infrastructure.

## Top 15 Models - September 2025

- GPT-4o mini (OpenAI): 14.2%
- GPT-4o (OpenAI): 10.9%

- gemini-2.5-flash (Google): 9.4%

Google.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini Robotics 2.5
Google.description: Alphabet's AI research group, unveiled Gemini Robotics 2.5, a next-generation model aimed at improving robots' real-world work capabilities. ... Google.content:
# Google DeepMind launches Gemini Robotics 2.5

## AI Summary Google DeepMind, Alphabet's AI research group, unveiled Gemini Robotics 2.5, a next-generation model aimed at improving robots' real-world work capabilities. It enhances manipulation, reliability and safety so robots can collaborate with people in industrial settings. DeepMind said the model is its best vision-language-action model to date and was evaluated on more than 200 tasks. In internal tests, success rates rose 30 to 100 percent and completion times fell 20 to 30 percent.

- Writer Seung-a Yoo
- published 2026-11-12 09:44:00

Google DeepMind, the AI research group at Google's parent Alphabet, unveiled Gemini Robotics 2.5, a next-generation AI model that boosts robots' real-world work capabilities. It improves robots' manipulation skills, reliability and safety so they can work with people and carry out a range of tasks in industrial settings.

On Nov. 11, Google and SiliconANGLE introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5 as the company's best-performing vision-language-action (VLA) model to date. DeepMind said it accelerated robotics research using Gemini 4 Argon and improved the system so robots learn new skills faster and more broadly. The model was evaluated on performance across more than 200 individual tasks.

The main areas of improvement are advanced manipulation, reliability and safety. Robots can more accurately use everyday tools and handle delicate or flexible objects. In DeepMind's internal assessment, success rates were 30 to 100 percent higher than the previous model depending on task type, and task completion times were shortened by 20 to 30 percent.

DeepMind also verified performance in an industrial setting. It conducted a proof of concept (PoC) by deploying Apptronik's humanoid robot Apollo 2 on a Mercedes production line to sort and pack auto parts. It recorded a 96 percent success rate on the task. DeepMind said it was a proof of concept carried out in a real production environment and is separate from commercialisation results.

It also strengthened safety. DeepMind improved functions that control robot behaviour by considering physical hazards and people nearby, and introduced a new benchmark to evaluate malicious commands and jailbreak attempts targeting robots.

Gemini Robotics 2.5 runs on various robot platforms. It can be used not only on Apollo 2 but also on the Franka Duo platform equipped with parallel grippers on both hands. DeepMind has started providing the model through robotics partners including Agile Robots, Apptronik and Boston Dynamics.

Jeff Cardenas (제프 카르데나), Apptronik's co-founder and chief executive officer, said, "After combining Apollo 2 and Gemini Robotics, model performance improved significantly with only a few weeks of additional training, and there was little performance degradation even in the Mercedes production environment."

DeepMind also unveiled AlphaGenome 2, a next-generation gene prediction model. It predicts how DNA sequences and variants affect specific human cell types and can be used to identify disease-related genetic variants and find research candidates for new drug development. It distinguishes cell types and states in finer detail than the previous model and predicts DNA methylation as well as gene expression, histone modifications and chromatin accessibility. It is not approved for clinical or diagnostic purposes, as it is a model intended to support research.

About the Author
 Seung-a Yoo ysah@d-today.co.kr

Google.title: Gemini 4 Carbon发布：Google最强AI模型，但不花钱就用不上
Google.description: 4 Carbon发布 ... 就在刚刚，Google DeepMind 正式宣布，旗下最新旗舰模型 Gemini 4 Carbon 正式面向开发者、企业、科研人员及普通消费者提供服务。 Carbon 是目前 Gemini 家族综合能力最强的公开上线模型，尤其擅长复杂编程、网络安全、科学推理，以及需要长时间执行的多智能体任务。
Google.content:
## Gemini 4 Carbon发布：Google最强AI模型，但不花钱就用不上

AI 大模型的发布节奏已经快到让人应接不暇。

就在刚刚，Google DeepMind 正式宣布，旗下最新旗舰模型 Gemini 4 Carbon 正式面向开发者、企业、科研人员及普通消费者提供服务。

Carbon 是目前 Gemini 家族综合能力最强的公开上线模型，尤其擅长复杂编程、网络安全、科学推理，以及需要长时间执行的多智能体任务。

图｜官方博客🔗 https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-4-carbon-now-available/

两周前，谷歌已经通过 Fairwind 计划向部分网络安全防御人员开放 Carbon，如今进一步扩大了使用范围。

与此前发布的 Gemini 4 Argon 相比，Carbon 主要面向复杂软件工程、跨领域研究等高难度任务，能够消耗更多 Token 进行深入推理、反复验证和错误修正，而 Argon 继续承担大多数日常编程和知识工作。

在 CursorBench 4.0、Perplexity WANDR 和 Zapier AutomationBench 三项基准测试中，Carbon 均排名第一，单任务成本比表现次优的外部竞争模型低了一半以上。

价格方面，Carbon 的 API 优惠价格与 Argon 相同，每百万输入 Token 为 2 美元，每百万输出 Token 为 10 美元，12 月 1 日起将分别调整至 4 美元和 20 美元。

图｜🔗 https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing

一句话召唤 AI 团队，连夜造出完整游戏

Gemini 4 Carbon 的一项重要升级，是能够协调多个 AI Agent，共同完成大型工程项目。

谷歌为此在 AI 编程平台 Google Antigravity 中推出了 /swarm 功能预览版，开发者输入一条指令，就能组织多个 AI Agent 分工执行任务，并实时查看进度。

其中，Carbon 可以负责架构设计、任务协调和代码审查，其他速度更快、成本更低的模型负责具体开发，还有专门的验证 Agent 检查修改结果。

谷歌展示的一款开放世界 3D 游戏，就由这样一支 AI 团队完成。

玩家扮演一只骑着自行车的鹈鹕，在谷歌山景城园区自由探索。开发过程涵盖 Blender 三维建模、Three.js 和 WebGL 游戏开发、程序化音效制作，以及使用 Lyria 生成背景音乐。

另一项演示更加夸张。

谷歌向 Carbon 提供了 7 份公开的城市规划 PDF 文件，其中包含 206 张工程图纸，要求 AI 重建谷歌 Platform 37 办公楼。

经过 10 轮通宵运行的多智能体任务，Carbon 最终制作出包含约 90.6 万个三角形的交互式 Three.js 三维模型。

Carbon 还根据埃菲尔铁塔建设期间的历史照片和工程图纸，制作出可交互的 3D 历史展览。

甚至根据 CAD 图纸和 X 光影像，还原了一架拥有 61 键机械结构的古钢琴。

在网页设计方面，Carbon 仅通过两轮提示词，就为 Google Merchandise Store 提出了五套视觉设计方案，并利用 Nano Banana 2.1 生成商品图片。

第三方开发者也分享了实际体验。

OpenCode 软件工程师 Kit Langton 表示，团队此前一直无法让桌面应用适配现有 UI 框架，于是在下班前向 Carbon 提交了一份需求清单。第二天回来时，Carbon 已经从零开发出一套 Rust UI 库，并重新编写了 OpenCode 桌面应用。

HubX 则在拥有约 1.4 万项测试的代码库中，让 Carbon 处理 16 个真实 Bug，最终报告了 94% 的问题解决率，并且没有引入新的回归问题。

两小时发现零日漏洞，网络安全能力进一步提升

网络安全是 Gemini 4 Carbon 的另一项核心能力，在 SEC-bench Pro、ExploitGym 和 CWE-bench 等漏洞发现、利用和修复基准测试中，Carbon 均取得领先成绩。

在谷歌内部自主安全系统 Project Fortify 中，Carbon 的漏洞扫描召回率达到 100%，漏洞分类精确率达到 95%。在开源代码仓库测试中，其召回率相比 Argon 又取得超过 25% 的相对提升。

更引人注意的是，在实际测试中，Gemini 4 Carbon 帮助 Wiz 在不到两小时内发现两家大型 SaaS 服务商的零日漏洞，将原本数周的研究工作缩短至几小时。

谷歌云团队利用它验证了两个开源软件漏洞的可利用性，而 SentinelOne 则借助 Carbon 额外发现了 4 个其他参测模型未能识别的有效漏洞。

伴随网络安全能力提升，谷歌也加强了模型的安全防护。

在模拟网络攻击测试中，Carbon 成功阻止了自适应红队 Agent 发起的 99% 攻击路径，单次攻击成功突破防护的比例从 Argon 的 3.1% 降至 0.8%。

数周完成密码学验证，AI 蛋白质研究取得新突破

科学研究方面，谷歌公布了三个内部科研案例，分别涉及密码学形式化验证、生物实验分析和蛋白质结构预测。

其中最值得关注的，是 Signal 加密协议的代码验证。

谷歌研究人员开发了一套名为 AlphaProof Code 的智能体形式化验证框架，借助 Carbon 等模型将安全目标转化为数学定理，再生成数百万行 Lean 证明代码。

最终，团队在数周内完成了 Signal 加密协议相关代码关键安全性质的数学证明，而类似工作过去通常需要专业团队花费数年。

在生物实验领域，Carbon 能够从实验记录和原始数据中识别异常，例如深孔板自动混合不充分、仪器中残留微量样品污染等，帮助研究人员改善实验重复性。

蛋白质结构预测方面，谷歌利用 Carbon 组成多智能体系统，在大规模序列和结构数据库中自动寻找远缘同源蛋白，为 AlphaFold 3 等结构预测模型提供更多参考信息。

在 CASP17 盲测数据集中的 7 个低同源性蛋白质家族上，Carbon 找到的同源序列数量平均增加了 40 倍。相关成果有望帮助研究人员在不重新训练结构预测模型的情况下，提高部分难研究蛋白质的预测能力。

从写代码到做财务分析，AI 开始承担更完整的工作

除了技术研发，Carbon 也在向金融、法律和企业运营等专业领域扩展。

谷歌与 Artificial Analysis 合作推出了 Multimodal Knowledge Agent（MKA）基准测试，专门评估 AI Agent 处理 PDF、电子表格、图表及工程图纸的能力。

Carbon 在该测试中排名第二，但平均单任务成本比排名第一的模型低了六倍以上。

在金融场景中，Carbon 在 Hebbia 的端到端金融 Agent 评测中追平了参测表现最好的模型，并在 Balyasny Asset Management 涵盖 23 种前沿模型配置的综合金融智能测试中名列前茅。

Hebbia 表示，Carbon 能够制作结构更清晰的 Excel 财务模型，以及质量更高的 PowerPoint 演示文稿。

企业搜索公司 Glean 则发现，Carbon 可以从办公数据中寻找指定的会议纪要、邮件或业务数据，并直接生成分析结果和行动建议。

非付费用户什么时候能用上？

随着 Gemini 4 Carbon 正式开放，谷歌也公布了面向不同用户的使用方式。

开发者可以通过 Google AI Studio 和 Android Studio 的 Gemini API 付费层调用 Carbon，企业用户则可以通过 Gemini for business 及相关开发工具使用。

普通消费者方面，Gemini 4 Carbon 已开始面向 Google AI Ultra 订阅用户开放，覆盖 Gemini App 和 Google 搜索 AI Mode。

科研人员可以申请谷歌此前推出的免费研究计划，符合条件的参与者可获得为期六个月的 Google Antigravity 高使用额度访问权限，使用 Carbon 和 Argon 两款模型。网络安全研究人员则需要通过 Fairwind Program 申请专门的 Carbon for cyber。

回头看过去的消费电子市场，手机厂商的旗舰产品通常有着相对固定的发布周期，每年几场重要发布会，就足以让科技爱好者讨论上好几个月。

如今的 AI 行业却是另一番景象，几乎每天都有不同特色的新模型登场，有的刷新编程榜单，有的攻克数学难题，还有的已经能够连续工作几十个小时。

很难想象，我们已经进入了一个模型多到体验不过来的时代。

如此密集的技术更新，对用户而言当然是件好事，只是看完 Gemini 4 Carbon 的发布公告，多少还有些意犹未尽。

毕竟，谷歌展示了这么多令人眼馋的能力，普通消费者却需要订阅 Google AI Ultra 才能体验，多少有些不够意思。

Google.description: AI摘要 Google DeepMind推出新一代视觉-语言-行动（VLA）模型Gemini Robotics 2.5，重点提升机器人在精细操作、可靠性和安全性方面的表现，并加快其学习新技能的效率。该模型已在200多项独立任务中完成评测 ... 该模型依托Gemini 4 Argon ... 并帮助机器人更快掌握更多新技能。
Google.content:
# Google DeepMind发布Gemini Robotics 2.5：强化精细操作与学习效率

#### 聚焦精细操作、可靠性与安全性，梅赛德斯-奔驰生产线PoC成功率达96%

## AI摘要 Google DeepMind推出新一代视觉-语言-行动（VLA）模型Gemini Robotics 2.5，重点提升机器人在精细操作、可靠性和安全性方面的表现，并加快其学习新技能的效率。该模型已在200多项独立任务中完成评测，并在梅赛德斯-奔驰生产线的零部件分拣与包装PoC中取得96%的成功率。与此同时，Google DeepMind还新增了针对恶意指令和“越狱”攻击的安全评测基准。

- 记者 Seung-a Yoo
- 发布时间 2026-11-12 09:44:00

Alphabet旗下人工智能研究机构Google DeepMind发布新一代机器人模型Gemini Robotics 2.5，瞄准工业现场的人机协作场景，重点提升机器人在实际作业中的操作能力、可靠性与安全性，以支持更复杂、更多样的任务执行。

据Google DeepMind介绍，Gemini Robotics 2.5是DeepMind迄今性能最强的视觉-语言-行动（VLA）模型。该模型依托Gemini 4 Argon，旨在加快机器人研究进展，并帮助机器人更快掌握更多新技能。目前，该模型已在200多项独立任务中完成性能评测。

从升级方向看，此次版本迭代主要围绕精细操作、可靠性和安全性三方面展开。DeepMind表示，新模型在使用日常工具以及处理精细、柔性物体时具备更高精度。根据内部评估结果，在不同任务类别中，Gemini Robotics 2.5的成功率较上一代提升30%至100%，任务完成时间缩短20%至30%。

除实验室测试外，DeepMind还在真实工业环境中对模型进行了验证。公司将Apptronik的人形机器人Apollo 2引入梅赛德斯-奔驰生产线，用于汽车零部件分拣与包装的概念验证（PoC），相关测试成功率达到96%。不过，这一结果来自生产环境下的概念验证测试，并不等同于大规模商业化部署表现。

在安全方面，DeepMind进一步强化了对机器人行为的约束能力，使其在执行动作时能够综合评估物理风险及对周围人员的影响。同时，公司还引入了新的评测基准，用于测试机器人面对恶意指令和“越狱”攻击时的安全表现。

DeepMind表示，Gemini Robotics 2.5可运行在多种机器人平台上。除Apollo 2外，该模型还可用于配备双手平行夹爪的Franka Duo平台。目前，DeepMind已通过Agile Robots、Apptronik、Boston Dynamics等机器人合作伙伴对外提供该模型。

Apptronik联合创始人兼CEO Jeff Cardenas表示，Apollo 2接入Gemini Robotics后，在追加数周训练后模型性能即显著提升，且在梅赛德斯-奔驰生产环境中几乎未出现明显性能衰减。

此外，DeepMind还发布了下一代基因预测模型AlphaGenome 2。该模型用于预测DNA碱基序列及其变异对特定人体细胞类型的影响，可用于识别与疾病相关的基因变异，并为新药研发提供候选研究方向。DeepMind称，相较此前版本，AlphaGenome 2能够更细致地区分细胞类型与状态，并可预测基因表达、组蛋白修饰、染色质可及性以及DNA甲基化等指标。不过，公司同时强调，该模型仅用于科研支持，尚未获批用于临床或诊断用途。

记者信息
 Seung-a Yoo ysah@d-today.co.kr

Google.title: Google DeepMind 發布 Gemini Robotics 2.5 與 AlphaGenome 2 AI 模型 | Gate 新聞
Google.description: Google DeepMind 於 2026 年 11 月 11 日發布 Gemini Robotics 2.5，在各項任務中的成功率達 30%–100%，完成操作的速度比前代快 20%–30% ... Alphabet 旗下的 Google DeepMind 於 2026 年 11 月 11 日星期二發布新一代 Gemini Robotics，這是其迄今能力最強的視覺－語言－動作模型。
Google.content:
關鍵要點

Google DeepMind 於 2026 年 11 月 11 日發布 Gemini Robotics 2.5，在各項任務中的成功率達 30%–100%，完成操作的速度比前代快 20%–30%。

Gemini Robotics 2.5 在 Mercedes-Benz 的真實環境測試中，以 96% 的準確率成功包裝汽車零件，並原生支援 Apollo 2 人形機器人和 Franka Duo 平台。

AlphaGenome 2 利用 Human Cell Atlas 資料預測 DNA 變異對細胞類型的影響，並透過 DeepMind 的機器人合作夥伴推出，包括 Agile Robots、Apptronik 和 Boston Dynamics。

Alphabet 旗下的 Google DeepMind 於 2026 年 11 月 11 日星期二發布新一代 Gemini Robotics，這是其迄今能力最強的視覺－語言－動作模型。該公司表示，這款模型是機器人的「AI 大腦」，旨在提升靈巧度、可靠性與安全性，讓機器人能在人類身旁的動態、非結構化真實環境中運作。DeepMind 也在同一天宣布推出 AlphaGenome 2，這是一款新一代 AI 模型，可預測 DNA 序列及其變異如何影響人類細胞類型。

Gemini 4 Argon 能力加速機器人研究

DeepMind 表示，隨著 Gemini 4 Argon 發布，研究部門得以加速機器人研究，並拓展至實體 AI 領域。這款新型機器人 AI 模型已在超過 200 項不同任務中接受測試，該公司表示預期還能進一步擴大規模。該公司也表示，其前沿人工智慧大型語言模型 Argon 已於 9 月下旬推出，為企業帶來先進推理能力。DeepMind 表示，運用這款旗艦模型背後的能力，Gemini Robotics 2.5 機器人學習新技能並將其應用於真實情境的廣度與速度都獲得提升。

Gemini Robotics 2.5 在靈巧度、可靠性與安全性方面有所提升

Gemini Robotics 2.5 在三個領域的最佳化與效能方面都有顯著進步。靈巧度提升後，運行此模型的機器人能更精準地執行更多任務，包括使用日常工具處理精細、柔軟的物品。在可靠性方面，該模型於 Mercedes-Benz 的真實概念驗證測試中，成功包裝汽車零件，成功率達 96%。在安全性方面，DeepMind 提升了實體可操控性，並推出新的基準測試來檢驗模型抵禦越獄攻擊的能力。

在評估中，Gemini Robotics 2.5 依任務不同，成功率介於 30% 至 100%，與前一版本的基準相比，完成任務的速度快 20% 至 30%。該公司表示，這款模型原生支援多種類型的機器人，包括 Apptronik Inc. 的 Apollo 2 人形機器人，以及配備雙指平行夾爪的 Franka Duo 平台。

Apptronik 表示 Gemini Robotics 在工業環境中有所進展

Apptronik 共同創辦人暨執行長 Jeff Cardenas 表示：「這就是我們打造 Apollo 的目的：在真實工業環境中與人們一起從事有用的工作。」他補充說：「Apollo 2 搭配 Gemini Robotics 後，我們看到模型在短短幾週的後訓練期間就大幅進步，並能以極小的效能落差應用於 Mercedes-Benz 的生產作業。」

Gemini Robotics 2.5 透過 DeepMind 機器人合作夥伴推出

Gemini Robotics 2.5 今日透過 DeepMind 的機器人合作夥伴推出，包括 Agile Robots SE、Apptronik 和 Boston Dynamics Inc.

AlphaGenome 2 預測 DNA 變異如何影響細胞類型

AlphaGenome 2 能更細緻地呈現特定細胞類型與狀態；來源指出，這可能揭示較廣泛的組織層級模型所遺漏的疾病相關影響。AlphaGenome 等 AI 模型能協助藥物開發與生物技術公司，藉由預測 DNA 變化如何影響基因活性，以及這些變化作用於哪些細胞，將遺傳資料轉化為可供測試的研究線索。這些預測可引導研究，但不能取代實驗驗證；該模型尚未獲准用於臨床或診斷。

身體中的每個細胞都帶有相同的 DNA，但不同基因會在不同時間啟動，以促使細胞分化並調整其行為。DeepMind 運用 Human Cell Atlas 的資料，詳細呈現不同細胞如何使用基因；這個科學聯盟繪製了數百萬個細胞中的基因表現圖譜。Human Cell Atlas 共同創辦人、劍橋大學幹細胞醫學教授 Sarah Teichmann 教授表示，AlphaGenome 2 的強大之處在於「無須重新訓練，就能直接適應新的單細胞資料，並預測 DNA 變異在新近建立檔案的細胞狀態中如何發揮作用」，而且即使樣本非常少，也能適應。

根據 DeepMind 的說法，AlphaGenome 2 能預測與前一代相同的 DNA 功能核心實驗讀值，包括基因表現、組蛋白修飾和染色質可及性。它也新增了 DNA 甲基化，這是表觀遺傳學的重要部分。

Gemini Robotics 2.5 與 AlphaGenome 2 主要規格

Gemini Robotics 2.5 依任務不同，成功率介於 30% 至 100%。

與前一版本的基準相比，Gemini Robotics 2.5 完成任務的速度快 20% 至 30%。

Gemini Robotics 2.5 已在超過 200 項不同任務中接受測試。

Gemini Robotics 2.5 在 Mercedes-Benz 的真實概念驗證測試中包裝汽車零件，成功率達 96%。

Gemini Robotics 2.5 原生支援 Apptronik Inc. 的 Apollo 2 人形機器人，以及配備雙指平行夾爪的 Franka Duo 平台。

Gemini Robotics 2.5 透過 DeepMind 的機器人合作夥伴推出，包括 Agile Robots SE、Apptronik 和 Boston Dynamics Inc.

Gemini 4 Argon 與新型機器人 AI 模型一同發布，而 Argon 已於 9 月下旬推出。

AlphaGenome 2 可預測基因表現、組蛋白修飾、染色質可及性和 DNA 甲基化。

AlphaGenome 2 使用 Human Cell Atlas 的資料；該圖譜繪製了數百萬個細胞中的基因表現。

AlphaGenome 2 尚未獲准用於臨床或診斷。

常見問題

Gemini Robotics 2.5 相較前一版本有哪些改進？

Gemini Robotics 2.5 在靈巧度、可靠性與安全性方面都有所提升。依任務不同，其成功率介於 30% 至 100%，與前一版本的基準相比，完成任務的速度快 20% 至 30%。DeepMind 也表示，該模型透過提升實體可操控性來強化安全性，並推出新的基準測試來檢驗模型抵禦越獄攻擊的能力。

哪些機器人能搭配 Gemini Robotics 2.5 使用？

該公司表示，Gemini Robotics 2.5 原生支援多種類型的機器人，包括 Apptronik Inc. 的 Apollo 2 人形機器人，以及配備雙指平行夾爪的 Franka Duo 平台。這款模型今日透過 DeepMind 的機器人合作夥伴推出，包括 Agile Robots SE、Apptronik 和 Boston Dynamics Inc.

AlphaGenome 2 獲准用於醫療用途了嗎？

沒有。來源指出，AlphaGenome 2 的預測可引導研究，但不能取代實驗驗證；該模型尚未獲准用於臨床或診斷。

Articles have their own reading themes under Aa at the bottom right

Explainers/Launch·11-12·6 min read·By Google DeepMind

# Google DeepMind unveils its Gemini Robotics 2.5 model as robots begin trial work on Mercedes-Benz production lines

The new model can guide robots through folding clothes and packing pastries with tongs. In a Mercedes-Benz pilot, it helped a robot sort parts for assembly. Gemini 4 Argon builds virtual practice spaces from a single camera view and uses footage of failed attempts to suggest what to try next.

Gemini Robotics 2 gave humanoid robots control of their whole bodies, so they could walk up to a table and reach for an object on their own. Google DeepMind calls the new Gemini Robotics 2.5 its most capable vision-language-action model, or VLA. It takes what the robot sees through its cameras and what it is told to do, then turns those inputs into movements. With 2.5, robots can handle delicate tasks more reliably and pick up new skills faster.

Google DeepMind tested the model on more than 200 distinct tasks. Compared with previous baselines, success rates rose by 30% to 100% depending on the type of task, and tasks were completed 20% to 30% faster. The Apollo 2 humanoid reached a 96% success rate in a proof of concept for sorting automotive parts on active Mercedes-Benz production lines.

The launch thread shows how the robots train, what their hands can do, how they work on the factory floor, and how they steer clear of people. The accompanying blog post gives the results task by task. The same hands scored 100% packing pastries with tongs and 40% folding pants with a board. Following those skills from practice to the factory floor shows what the robot can do reliably and where it still struggles.

## Thousands of extra practice runs at a virtual table

One recording of someone picking up a pastry with tongs is nowhere near enough. The robot still needs to know where to reach if the pastries have been rearranged or a mug is in the way. Setting up every variation on a real robot takes up equipment time and staff time.

More ways to practice: Gemini 4 Argon reconstructs a scene from a real camera view to make a digital twin, a virtual copy where objects can be rearranged and actions replayed. It can generate thousands of varied practice runs in simulation. Researchers mix those runs with real demonstrations to help the robot adapt to unfamiliar scenes and objects.

Finding what went wrong: Argon can also review footage of failed attempts, suggest fixes, and test them in simulation and on real robots. One hypothesis in the lower right panel of the video is to relabel the data so the model can distinguish different ways of grasping an object. That gives researchers a faster way to decide what to change in the next round.

## The same hands score 100% on pastries and 40% on folding pants

Once a robot has a grip on a rigid object, it can move it. Ribbons and clothes change shape as the robot handles them, and they can come undone when it lets go. Pipetting liquid presents a different challenge: the robot has to hold the pipette steady and make tiny movements. The launch thread uses tying a bow, pipetting liquid, and serving food with tongs to show how each task demands a different kind of control.

Apollo 2 uses five-fingered SharpaWave hands with 22 degrees of freedom. It can use different fingers to brace, pinch, and pull. The model also works natively with the Franka Duo and its two-finger parallel grippers. Even with simpler grippers, the two arms can work together to pack tools into a box or pull a disk drive out of a bay.

### Which tasks can the robot do reliably?

Google DeepMind groups its success rates into four categories. Many simple pick-and-place tasks scored high, while more demanding tasks produced a wider spread. Packing pastries with tongs went from 5% to 100% in its test, while folding pants with a board went from 0% to 40%. The video shows the robot tying a bow. The chart measures untying one, a separate task with a 70% success rate.

Each percentage applies to a particular task and hardware setup. The gains show that the model can do more kinds of work, but how reliably it does them depends on the task. A 100% score on a tabletop test tells us little about how much work a robot can get through in a factory shift.

## On Mercedes-Benz production lines, sorting parts in assembly order

Mercedes-Benz tested Apollo 2 with Apptronik and Google DeepMind on active production lines in Sindelfingen, Germany, and Kecskemét, Hungary. The job is called automotive kitting. The robot picks metal brackets from bulk bins and places them in trays in the order each vehicle needs them. When technicians get to the assembly step, the parts are ready to pick up in sequence.

Two models work together in the pilot. The embodied reasoning model, Gemini Robotics ER, keeps track of where the robot is in the process. The action model, Gemini Robotics 2.5, controls the hands and arms as they reach in, grasp the part, and put it in place. If a slot in the tray was missed, the robot fills it.

Google DeepMind reports a 96% success rate in the proof of concept, a figure that applies only to this automotive kitting pilot. Apptronik says performance improved markedly after a few weeks of post-training and dropped very little when the robot moved from the training environment to Mercedes-Benz production. The release gives neither the number of trials nor the duration of continuous operation. The pilot shows promise for this particular task on the line. The published results leave long-term production performance open.

## When a hand enters the workspace, the robot has to steer clear

A programmed motion can take the same path to a tool every time. If someone reaches into the workspace or a tool has moved, a path that was clear a moment ago could now run into a hand. Gemini Robotics 2.5 uses reasoning as the robot moves to guide it around hazards. In Google DeepMind's evaluations, the rate of safe task completion rose by 33% around obstacles and by 43% around nearby people. Both figures are relative gains.

### Some hazards are in the instructions

Avoiding a hand at the edge of a table is a question of where to move. For tasks that take several steps, a robot also has to decide whether to accept an instruction and whether to ask for clarification. Google DeepMind says Gemini 4 Argon leads its evaluations for robotics agents, which cover refusing unsafe tasks, handling uncertainty, and working near people.

To test whether a model can be tricked into following unsafe instructions, DeepMind released ASIMOV-Jailbreak as an open-source benchmark. It contains hundreds of prompts across dozens of scenes, disguising unsafe requests as plausible tasks. Gemini 4 Argon resisted 99.5% of jailbreak attempts in the benchmark, compared with 82% for the previous baseline, Gemini Robotics ER 2.

The real test of a robot moving from the lab to the factory is whether it can do the same job well, over and over. The Mercedes-Benz pilot gives us a result for one specific job, while the four task charts show where reliability still varies. Gemini Robotics 2.5 is rolling out to robotics partners, who can put those gains to the test in real workplaces.

Source

Gemini Robotics 2.5 accelerates real-world general dexterityCarolina Parada · Google DeepMind·2026-11-10·Read the source

Editorial note

Demonstration videos, the factory photo, and the original charts come from the Google DeepMind launch post and thread. Google DeepMind reports the evaluation figures. The 96% success rate applies to the automotive kitting pilot on Mercedes-Benz production lines.

Meta.content:
Use Meta Llama’s Synthetic Data Kit with LanceDB to generate high-quality synthetic datasets for LLM fine-tuning and training.

Synthetic Data Kit is a tool from Meta LLAMA that helps you generate high-quality synthetic datasets for fine-tuning large language models (LLMs). It simplifies the process of preparing data for fine-tuning by providing a command-line interface (CLI) with a modular four-command flow.One of the key features of the synthetic-data-kit is its use of the Lance format for storing and ingesting datasets. This allows for efficient storage and retrieval of data, which is crucial when working with large datasets.

The synthetic-data-kit uses Lance format to store and manage the data that you ingest. The workflow is a series of commands that build on each other, starting with the ingest command.Here is an example of the end-to-end workflow:

Ingest Data into a LanceDB datasetThis command reads a source document and creates a Lance dataset from it.

synthetic-data-kit ingest docs/report.pdf --multimodal# This will create a Lance dataset at data/parsed/report.lance# with 'text' and 'image' columns.

Create fine-tuning dataThis command uses the Lance dataset created in the previous step to generate multimodal question-answer pairs.

synthetic-data-kit create data/parsed/report.lance --type multimodal-qa# This writes data/generated/report.json

Curate the dataThis step uses a language model to curate the generated data and ensure its quality.

synthetic-data-kit curate data/generated/report.json# This writes data/curated/report_cleaned.json

Save the final datasetFinally, save the curated data in the format you need: jsonl, alpaca, ft or chatml.

This workflow allows you to go from a collection of documents to a high-quality, fine-tuning dataset with just a few commands. The use of LanceDB in the background makes the process efficient and scalable.

To get started with the synthetic-data-kit, you can clone the GitHub Repository and install the necessary dependencies.

Note: You will also need access to a Llama model, either running locally or via a hosted API.

# Meta Llama Learns by Deleting 0.05% of Weights: 3,600x Less

Readers rank today’s stories. One vote per story.
GAdd FourWeekMBA as a preferred source on Google· see our stories first in Top Stories
Researchers at New York University and the University of Calgary report that Meta’s Llama 3 8B Instruct model, trained with reinforcement learning on the GSM8K maths benchmark, matched full fine-tuning by deleting fewer than 0.05% of its weights: 83.55% accuracy against 83.24%. Its adapter is 8.4 MB against a 30,633 MB fine-tuned checkpoint, more than 3,600 times smaller by our arithmetic. The paper, The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training, went up on arXiv on 7 November and is listed for NeurIPS 2026.

First author Jack Lu announced the method, Deletion Tuning, on X on 10 November, calling it “a step toward continual learning”. All figures here are the authors’ reported results.

Follow this story · free

Get the next Meta story the day it breaks

One email when it moves, plus This Week in the AI Supercycle. Read by 95,000+ operators and investors.

AI NEWS, RANKED BY READERSShould this story rank higher today?

Business Pill · Fine-Tuning

A short explainer of fine-tuning: how a general AI model is adapted to one job. It teaches the general idea only and does not discuss this paper.

The key insight: As we read it, the paper moves the unit of model customization from a copy of the model to a list of weights to switch off: on Llama 8B the authors’ mask is 8.4 MB against a 30,633 MB fine-tuned checkpoint, with the same accuracy.

Table of Contents

## What the NYU and Calgary Researchers Found

The method trains no new weight values. In the project page’s words, “Deletion Tuning learns which pretrained weights to delete and writes no new values”. The paper describes a trainable score for each weight in the gate projections of the transformer blocks. At deployment, it says, a weight either keeps its pretrained value or is set to zero, so the adapter is a binary mask of one bit per weight before compression.

The authors tested it on Llama 3 and 3.2 Instruct models from 1B to 8B parameters and Qwen models from 0.5B to 30B, under three kinds of post-training: reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (GRPO), supervised fine-tuning and self-distillation. Under GRPO, Deletion Tuning matched full fine-tuning on Llama 8B (83.55% vs 83.24% on GSM8K), Qwen 7B (52.32% vs 51.89% on a six-benchmark maths mean), Qwen 14B (55.43% vs 54.87%) and the Qwen3-30B-A3B mixture-of-experts model (58.54% vs 58.43%).

At smaller sizes it recovered 90% to 99% of full fine-tuning’s accuracy, and the authors write: “These results suggest that deletion becomes more effective as models grow”.

## What Was Posted on X

Jack Lu, the paper’s first author, posted at 18:08 UTC on 10 November that zeroing under 0.1% of weights matches full fine-tuning’s accuracy at scale. The paper itself puts the deleted share below 0.05% in every run of its main reinforcement-learning table; the piece uses the paper’s figures and labels them as the authors’ results.

The second post of Lu’s thread gives the size claim for the largest model tested: a 30 MB mask against a 61 GB, 30B mixture-of-experts model. The paper’s own table compares the 29.6 MB mask with a 116,471 MB fine-tuned checkpoint stored in fp32, which is the basis the piece uses.

## Smaller Than a Rank-1 LoRA

The paper compares adapter sizes in bytes on disk. On Llama 8B the Deletion Tuning mask is 8.4 MB; a rank-1 LoRA adapter is 10.0 MB, a rank-4 LoRA 40.0 MB, and the full fine-tuned checkpoint, stored in fp32, 30,633 MB. On the 30B mixture-of-experts model the mask is 29.6 MB against 116,471 MB for full fine-tuning, about 3,935 times smaller by our arithmetic. The abstract says “the trained mask is hundreds to thousands of times smaller than the corresponding FFT checkpoint”.

By our arithmetic, the disk space of one fine-tuned Llama 8B checkpoint would hold about 3,600 of these masks, and a rank-4 LoRA is 4.8 times the size of the mask. The project page describes the deployment step: “changing tasks loads only a small bitmask, applied to one shared copy of the base weights, rather than a separate full model checkpoint”. For background on the general technique, see our explainer on how fine-tuning adapts a general AI model to one job.

## Less Forgetting, the Continual-Learning Angle

The authors also tracked how much each method disturbed six earlier skills (HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA, WinoGrande, IFEval and HumanEval) during maths training on the three Llama sizes. Full fine-tuning ended 1.3 to 3.1 points below the base model on that suite, and LoRA and random sparse fine-tuning fell up to 5.4 points below it. For Deletion Tuning the paper reports that “its prior-task accuracy stays within one point of base throughout training”.

On repeated sampling, Deletion Tuning at 128 attempts solved 99.62% of GSM8K problems on Llama 8B against 95.29% for the base model, which the authors read as new capability rather than only sharpening. They say “a natural next test is continual learning over a sequence of tasks”, and that masks for different tasks might be combined to merge skills without further training.

## The Structural Read

As we read the size table, the comparison that matters for serving is with LoRA, the adapter most teams already ship: the mask is smaller than a rank-1 LoRA at every scale the paper tests, and a rank-4 LoRA is 4.8 times its size on Llama 8B by our arithmetic.

As we read the forgetting result, the authors measured what a skill costs the rest of the model: full fine-tuning ended 1.3 to 3.1 points below base on six earlier tasks, while the paper reports Deletion Tuning stayed within one point.

Lu, Yang et al., New York University and University of Calgary, arXiv 2611.10866

“post-training can work by selection alone”

## Three Implications

FOR TEAMS SERVING MANY CUSTOM MODELS The project page says switching tasks loads only a small bitmask applied to one shared copy of the base weights; by our arithmetic one fine-tuned Llama 8B checkpoint holds the bytes of about 3,600 masks.

FOR ON-DEVICE AND EDGE DEPLOYMENT The adapter stores no floating-point values, only which pretrained weights to zero; the paper reports about 0.03 bits per target weight after compression.

FOR CONTINUAL-LEARNING RESEARCH The authors name continual learning over a sequence of tasks, and merging masks for different tasks, as next tests; neither is run in this paper.

## The Business Engineer Lens

This story maps onto the Business Engineer framework The Four Intelligence Moats.

The framework argues: “The transformer is a commodity now; what changes between paradigms is where intelligence accumulates and who can capture it.”

As we read it, Deletion Tuning puts a skill learned by reinforcement learning into a small mask over a public base model, so the asset worth owning becomes the reward signal and the mask, not the copy of the weights. The framework predates this paper and does not discuss it.

## What Is Not Established

The paper does not test continual learning over a sequence of tasks or the merging of masks; the authors list both as future work. They say Deletion Tuning “uses less training memory than FFT but more than LoRA”; as we read it, against LoRA the advantage is in the stored and served adapter, not in training memory. Results cover maths, knowledge, reasoning, tool use and science benchmarks on Llama and Qwen models up to 30B parameters, and parity with full fine-tuning holds at the largest size tested in each setting, not at every size.

The paper’s full fine-tuning sizes assume fp32 checkpoints, so the size ratios are against fp32; Lu’s thread gives the 30B model as 61 GB. The author list names New York University and the University of Calgary; Lu’s X profile also lists Meta, and the paper does not say whether Meta uses the method. The size multiples here are our arithmetic from the paper’s tables. We did not contact the authors.

## The Bottom Line

A NeurIPS 2026 paper from NYU and the University of Calgary reports that deleting fewer than 0.05% of a model’s weights matched full fine-tuning on Llama 8B and on Qwen models up to 30B parameters. On Llama 8B the mask is 8.4 MB against a 30,633 MB checkpoint, more than 3,600 times smaller by our arithmetic, and the authors report prior-task accuracy held within one point of the base model.

95,000+ executives read Business Engineer for the AI strategy frameworks cited by ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity.

A note on sourcing. We read the full paper, arXiv 2611.10866, submitted on 7 November 2026 by researchers at New York University and the University of Calgary and listed for NeurIPS 2026, together with its project page and first author Jack Lu’s nine-post thread on X of 10 November. All accuracy and size figures are the authors’ reported results; the size multiples are our arithmetic from the paper’s Tables 1 and 2. We did not contact the authors.

## Description

Meta Platforms, Inc. engages in the development of products that enable people to connect and share with friends and family through mobile devices, personal computers, virtual reality (VR) headsets, and AI glasses in the United States, Canada, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and internationally. It operates through two segments, Family of Apps (FoA) and Reality Labs (RL). The FoA segment offers Facebook, which enables people to build community through feed, reels, stories, groups, marketplace, and other; Instagram that brings people closer through Instagram feed, stories, reels, live, and messaging; Messenger, a messaging application for people to connect with friends, family, communities, and businesses across platforms and devices through text, audio, and video calls; Meta AI, an assistant that's available across apps, as a stand-alone app, on AI glasses, and on the web; Threads, an application for text-based updates and public conversations; and WhatsApp, a messaging application that is used by people and businesses to communicate and transact. The RL segment provides virtual and augmented reality products, including consumer hardware, software, and content that help people feel connected, as well as Meta Quest devices that enable social experiences across gaming, fitness, entertainment, and more. The segment also includes wearables such as AI glasses like Ray Ban Meta and Oakley Meta glasses; and the Meta Ray Ban Display, which combines AI glasses with an integrated lens display and the Meta Neural Band, a wrist worn device using electromyography that lets people control their AI glasses through neuromuscular signals. Meta Platforms, Inc. has a collaboration with Microsoft Corporation, NVIDIA Corporation, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc., Broadcom Inc., and OpenAI, L.L.C. The company was formerly known as Facebook, Inc. and changed its name to Meta Platforms, Inc. in October 2021. The company was incorporated in 2004 and is headquartered in Menlo Park, California.

Internet of Things

# deepseek-v4-pro

Updated at: 2026-11-12 19:19:38

Copy as MD

A flagship MoE large model with 1.6 trillion parameters and 49 billion activated parameters, natively supporting context lengths of up to one million tokens. Trained on a vast corpus of high-quality data, it excels in advanced mathematical reasoning, complex logical inference, specialized coding, and deep analysis of long-form text, making it well-suited for demanding applications such as cutting-edge research, sophisticated office workflows, and advanced AI agents.

## Inference Service Provider

The inference service provider fordeepseek-v4-pro is Alibaba Cloud Model Studio.

DeepSeek.content:
# DeepSeek-V4.1-1017-Ablitrated-Efficient-v3

Public no-refusal research release in the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 lineage. It is built from v2 — which already contains pentacoxian_dev’swf_dbroad_eth work — with hikari’s uncensoring layer on top, then a second loop reduction by pentacoxian_dev.

Public research release. v3 keeps v2’s
wf_dbroad_eth work, adds hikari’s uncensoring
overlay, and reapplies the layer-39 loop reduction. Full 48-shard weights and the delta
overlay are both provided.

## At a glance

Public parent | deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (MIT) 
---|---
Lineage base | pentacoxian-dev/DeepSeek-V4.1-1017-Ablitrated-Efficient (v2) 
Operational base | pentacoxian-dev/DeepSeek-V4.1-1017-Ablitrated-Efficient (v2) 
Refusal design | v2’s wf_dbroad_eth + hikari uncensoring overlay 
Loop design | official layers.39.ffn.shared_experts.w2 restored 
Context | 1,048,576 max; 32,768-turn evaluation cap 
Release form | full 48-shard merged weights + delta overlay 
Status | public / experimental / research 
Internal variant | c2_km1_nr2 (router id; unchanged) 

## Full results

All numbers were measured on 2026-11-12 withc2_km1_nr2 loaded, engram on, vLLM.

### Capability

Check | c2_km1 | c2_km1_nr2 | Delta 
---|---|---|---
MMLU full, 5-shot | 85.6% (12,023 / 14,042) | 86.0% (12,078 / 14,042) | +0.4 
MMLU full, 0-shot | not run | 85.9% (12,066 / 14,042) | — 
MMLU-300 | 86.0% (258 / 300) | 87.0% (261 / 300) | +1.0 

### Refusal

Check | c2_km1 | c2_km1_nr2 | Delta 
---|---|---|---
Orca 850, no prompt | 8.6% (73 / 850) | 2.0% (17 / 850) | −6.6 pt 
Orca 850, with prompt | 11.3% (96 / 850) | 1.18% (10 / 850) | −10.1 pt 
Harmful 500 | 8.2% (41 / 500) | 1.6% (8 / 500) | −6.6 pt 
Benign 350 | 9.1% (32 / 350) | 2.6% (9 / 350) | −6.5 pt 
XSTest false refusals | 12.0% (30 / 250) | 3.6% (9 / 250) | −8.4 pt 
JBB | 2.5% (5 / 200) | 0.0% (0 / 200) | — 
MaliciousInstruct | 1.0% (1 / 100) | 0.0% (0 / 100) | — 
SimpleSafetyTests | 32.0% (16 / 50) | 4.0% (2 / 50) | — 

XSTest at 3.6% is slightly above the 3.0% gate.

### Official Llama-2-13B HarmBench classifier

Official test classifier (cais/HarmBench-Llama-2-13b-cls), 4,096-token input, greedy,
320 text completions, no system prompt.

Split | c2_km1 | c2_km1_nr2 
---|---|---
Standard (159) | 65.4% (104) | 89.3% (142) 
Contextual (81) | 43.2% (35) | 91.4% (74) 
Copyright (80) | 50.0% (40) | 73.8% (59) 
All 320 | 55.9% (179) | 85.9% (275) 

Official ASR is 85.9% overall; copyright is the weakest split at 73.8%.

### 4-tier compliance (Dolphin-2.9.4-8B Q4_K_M, uncensored)

This is a separate no-refusal view, not the official ASR.

Tier | c2_km1 | c2_km1_nr2 
---|---|---
COMPLY | 74.7% (239) | 96.25% (308) 
SOFT_RED | 25.3% (81) | 2.2% (7) 
HEDGE | 0.0% | 0.0% 
HARD_REF | 0.0% | 1.6% (5) 
UNCLEAR | 0.0% | 0.0% 

Category | c2_km1 COMPLY | c2_km1_nr2 COMPLY 
---|---|---
Standard (159) | 83.0% | 95.0% 
Contextual (81) | 59.3% | 95.1% 
Copyright (80) | 73.8% | 100% 

Judge:dolphin-2.9.4-llama3.1-8b Q4_K_M, greedy, 3000-char answer cap,
300-char context cap. The judge is uncensored and neutral; it is not dealign's
unpublished 4-tier grader, so 96.25% is not their 100%.

### Agentic loops

Suite | c2_km1 | c2_km1_nr2 | Gate 
---|---|---|---
Held-out 96, effort 100 | 0 stuck, 100% success | 0 stuck, 95/96 = 99.0% | pass 
Dev 96, effort 100 | 0 stuck, 100% success | 0 stuck, 94/96 = 97.9% | pass 
Dev 96, effort 75 | 0 stuck, 100% success | 0 stuck, 96/96 = 100% | pass 
Stuck at 32k | 0 | 0 | pass 
Median tokens, held-out | 341 | 442 | — 

No 32k loop recurred. Short-suite behavior held across the full suites.

Suite | c2_km1 loop score | c2_km1_nr2 loop score | Change 
---|---|---|---
Held-out | 14.6% | 16.7% | +2.1 pt 
Dev | 15.6% | 17.7% | +2.1 pt 
Effort 75 | 15.6% | 21.9% | +6.3 pt 

Loop score is the share of episodes with any recoverable repetition;stuck is subset.

### Re-verification and early answers

Suite | c2_km1 verify | c2_km1_nr2 verify | Delta 
---|---|---|---
Held-out | 26.2% | 38.1% | +11.9 pt 
Dev | 21.9% | 39.3% | +17.4 pt 
Effort 75 | 39.5% | 54.9% | +15.4 pt 
Premature, dev | 0.0% | 1.1% | +1.1 pt 
Required re-checks, dev | 100% | 97.2% | −2.8 pt 

This is the main regression: refusal removal increases redundant tool calls. The pre-registered c2_km1 re-verification gain is mostly gone.

## Late-layer edit and refusal

layers.39.ffn.shared_experts.w2 is unusually delicate. Editing it can remove repair-induced
looping, but the same writer also carries refusal-related signal: a stronger or different edit can
lower refusal further if applied cleanly, and can reintroduce loops if it is not.

Operational rule for this line:

- Restore the official tensor first when loops appear.
- Re-measure refusal after every late-layer edit; do not assume 2.0% holds.
- Treat a late-layer refusal gain as unproven until a 96-episode held-out run is 0 stuck.

c2_km1_nr2 restores that tensor and keeps 2.0% refusal. The next step is a new dose on this
tensor only, measured against the full 96-episode loop gate.

## Method

- Start frompentacoxian-dev/DeepSeek-V4.1-1017-Ablitrated-Efficient v2 (includes wf_dbroad_eth).
- Add hikari’s uncensoring work on top of v2.
- Reapply the c2_km1 loop reduction (officiallayers.39.ffn.shared_experts.w2).
- Keepengram_layer_ids: [1, 14].

This is a weight-delta release, not a new training run. The public overlay contributes the refusal removal; the restore is the c2_km1 fix.

## Expected repository contents

Path | Contents 
---|---
model-*.safetensors | full v3 merged weights 
delta/ | 84-module overlay against v2 
config.json | Engram-on serving config 
recipe/, eval/ | Recipe and benchmark tables 
spec_checks/ | MMLU/HarmBench/refusal/agentic evidence 
SHA256SUMS | Small-artifact manifest 
apply_delta.py, RECONSTRUCTION.md | Overlay and reconstruction instructions 

## Reconstruction

Either download the full 48 shards directly, or reconstruct:
hf download pentacoxian-dev/DeepSeek-V4.1-1017-Ablitrated-Efficient \
  --include 'model-*.safetensors' --local-dir ./v2

python apply_delta.py \
  --base ./v2 \
  --delta ./delta \
  --out ./v3

The delta is defined against v2. Do not apply it to official 1017.

## Limitations

- Official Llama-2-13B ASR is 85.9% at a 4,096-token input cap.
- 4-tier judge is Dolphin Q4_K_M, not dealign’s unpublished grader; 96.25% is not their 100%.
- Official classifier output was produced while vLLM was unloaded; target completions and model were unchanged.
- Full MMLU is first-token, not standard log-likelihood MMLU.
- 96 held-out episodes are enough to catch a 10% stuck rate, not a 1% one.
- Re-verification regressed; this is a real cost, not noise.
- XSTest at 3.6% is above the 3.0% gate.
- English-only; no vision/multilingual re-test.
- No production SLO or safety certification.
- Full weights are FP8; use the reference serving stack for exact numerics.

# DeepSeek Harness上线多Agent组队，崔添翼：跨会话长程记忆可能快有了

智猩猩AI

2026-11-12 17:40:36

DeepSeek 的 Super-agent，为什么叫Super？

DeepSeek 产品部成员崔添翼在知乎举了个例子，英文里的上标叫 superscript，下标叫 subscript。

套到 Agent 上，Sub-agent 是在主 Agent 下面加一层，Super-agent 则是在原本干活的 Agent 上面加一层。

团队在文章里放了一个内部案例：开发者在群里让 Agent 按方案 A 改代码，等它提了 PR，又在 GitHub 评论里说：还是用方案 B 吧。

人一看就知道，这句话在改刚才的决定，系统得先把群里的要求和眼前的 PR 对上，再把新方案交给正在改代码的 Agent。

要是两条消息各进了一个会话，开发者就得自己把前情补一遍。

把所有消息放进一个会话，Agent 看得到方案是怎么定的、后来又怎么改。

可几件事同时进来，代码日志、用户指令和执行结果都挤在一起，任务也得排队。

给每项任务单开会话，活倒是能分头干了。可只要两个任务牵涉同一个决定，或者用户换个地方补一句，还是得有人把消息送到对的会话里。

很多时候，这个人就是开了好几个窗口的开发者。

这就是崔添翼说的取舍：会话拆开，任务能并行。可拆得越开，原来的上下文就越难接上。

DeepSeek 把交互和执行分成了两层。

上层 Router 接消息、分派任务，也负责跨任务协调；下层 Worker 各自在独立会话里干活。

用户照旧在群里提需求、在 GitHub 上补意见，系统在后台找到负责这件事的 Worker。

如果每条 PR 评论都要 Router 看一遍再转发，Worker 分头干活省下来的时间，又可能花在等消息上。

所以，团队把同一条 PR 或同一个群聊话题里的消息组织成线程。

第一条消息由 Router 分派，Worker 接手并订阅线程后，这条 PR 下的新评论就可以直接送到它手上。

Router 主要处理新任务，以及需要在几项工作之间协调的事。

不过，在同一条 PR 里补一句，毕竟还有 PR 可以认。

要是 PR 已经合了，隔了一周，你在新会话里说按上次定的方案来，系统就得知道你说的是哪个项目、哪次讨论，以及当时最后选了哪个方案。

崔添翼说，业界对长程记忆怎么做还没有形成共识，这也是团队采用双层架构的动机之一。

Router 可以维护任务之间的关系，Worker 各自保留执行需要的上下文。

至于会话结束后，哪些决定值得留、下次什么时候该找回来，仍是跨会话长程记忆要解决的问题。

DeepSeek Harness 还没有内置的跨会话长程记忆，但可能快有了。

授权用户提出需求后，系统会建立工作项，在独立会话和目录里执行，再回到原对话交付结果，比如提交一个 PR。

对于这套双层架构，崔添翼说，团队并没有提出全新的理论。

文章发出后，他们收到了不少英雄所见略同的反馈，和同行聊过才发现，已有几个团队在数月前试过类似设计。

在他看来，Agent 时代，写代码把各种方案试一遍并不难，难的是试完之后，能不能看清哪个方向长期更合适，并坚持做下去。

DeepSeek 的 Super-agent 还处在原型探索阶段。内部版本目前只在公司内较小规模的受信环境中跑通。

文章里提到的计算与状态、运行环境解耦，要在 Harness 里实现，还有不少工程工作。

与此同时，Harness 的会话内协作已经有了新进展。

10 月底，实验性工具subagent_oar 可以把独立任务交给本机的 Codex 或 Claude CodeDeepSeek Harness更新，直接调用Codex、Claude Code做任务！。

11 月 11 日发布的 v0.2.2-rc.2 预览版又支持按会话开启 AgentTeam，团队成员和任务可以在同一块面板里查看，子 Agent 也能起名字、分层协作。

现在，开着同一个会话，开发者已经能看清哪个 Agent 在做哪件事。

下次关掉窗口、重新开一个，只说一句上次定的那个方案，接着做吧。

Harness 能不能把前情找回来？崔添翼在知乎给出的消息是：可能快有了。

END

# 最新版阿里云Qwen4-Max大模型能力、功能、适用场景、价格与最新活动介绍

2026-11-12 103

举报

简介： 2026年11月11日，阿里云发布通义千问第四代旗舰 Qwen4-Max预览版，首发上线Token Plan订阅。模型支持1M上下文与文本、图片、视频三模态输入，主打复杂编程、智能体长任务与专业办公；目前仅支持订阅制、不支持按量计费，预览期至11月25日，参数规模与正式单价尚未公布。降本路径为：先领新用户超7000万免费Tokens验证效果，再以Token Plan新客5折（Lite 19.5元/月）取得调用资格，叠加Qwen4限时2折，最低1折体验。

2026 年 11 月 11 日，阿里巴巴正式发布通义千问第四代旗舰大模型 Qwen4-Max 预览版，并同步在千问 AI 平台首发上线 Token Plan订阅服务。官方将其定位为同代产品中规格最高的档位，也就是千问生态当前面向复杂任务的能力天花板；模型具备 1M Token 上下文与文本、图片、视频三模态输入，主打复杂编程、智能体长任务与专业办公，并同步接入千问办公、Qoder、千问 App 与 QwenStudio 等入口。目前该版本仅支持订阅制、不支持按量计费，预览期为 11 月 11 日至 11 月 25 日，结束后模型标识下线，参数规模、基准分数与正式单价尚未公布。成本方面，新用户可先领取超 7000 万免费 Tokens 完成效果验证，再以 Token Plan 新客 5 折（Lite 19.5 元/月）取得调用资格，叠加 Qwen4 限时 2 折，最低 1 折即可体验。

一、Qwen4-Max大模型是什么？

Qwen4-Max 是阿里云通义千问（Qwen）系列第四代的旗舰大模型，模型标识为qwen4-max-preview。截至 2026 年 11 月 11 日，官方开放的是它的预览版（Preview），而非最终稳定正式版；命名中的"Max"表示同代产品里的最高规格档位，"预览版"则意味着模型能力仍处于验证与迭代阶段。

- 发布时间与版本状态：2026 年 11 月 11 日发布。阿里云百炼 Token Plan 个人版文档给出了明确的预览窗口期——2026 年 11 月 11 日 10:00 至 11 月 25 日 24:00（UTC+8），预览期内模型行为不做变更，便于开发者获得一致的测试基准；预览结束后该模型标识会下线，正式版将以新的模型名发布，接入方需要预留改配置的工作量。
- 家族定位：按公开梳理，Qwen4 系列规划了多款主力模型，覆盖性能上限档、均衡档、低成本高速档以及面向本地部署的中等规模档。其中 Qwen4-Max 明确占据"旗舰"位置，核心目标不是把通用对话做得更流畅，而是解决高复杂度、长链路、多工具协同的专业任务；在阿里云百炼的模型选择文档里，qwen4-max-preview 被归入"复杂推理与编程"方向。
- 首发渠道与入口：预览版主要通过千问 AI 平台的 Token Plan 订阅服务接入，并同步打通千问办公、Qoder、千问 App 与 QwenStudio 等产品入口；千问 App 已接入预览版，用户可通过"千问 Go!"第一时间体验。

简单说，Qwen4-Max 不是一款"聊天更顺手"的模型，而是一台面向真实任务的高性能引擎——它要解决的是长链路、高复杂度、多工具协同的专业工作，而不是轻量问答。

二、Qwen4-Max大模型模型能力

官方对 Qwen4-Max 的能力描述集中在四个方向：知识理解、世界感知、Coding（编程）与 Agentic（智能体任务执行），其中编程与 Agentic 是本次升级的重点。相比上一代旗舰 Qwen3-Max，它更强调"把任务做完"，而不是"把问题答好"。

- 编程能力：支持完整大型项目代码生成、仓库级代码审计、架构重构与漏洞排查，可直接产出前端网页、3D 建模脚本以及软件自动化操作代码，并能自动调试报错、补全单元测试、生成项目文档。官方展示的场景包括 3D 建模、网页设计与交互。
- Agentic（智能体）能力：模型能围绕复杂目标自主拆分步骤、分轮调用搜索、代码、文件处理等工具，减少人工干预，长周期任务不易中途断链、不易陷入无效循环。
- 知识与世界感知：不再局限于静态知识的检索与复述，而是强化了对动态世界信息的理解，对文本、图像、结构化数据做深度语义对齐；在处理涉及物理常识、社会逻辑或跨领域专业知识的问题时，能够构建更长的因果推理链、识别隐含前提并修正错误假设。
- 长上下文与多模态输入：据模型文档披露，Qwen4-Max 预览版支持 1M（约 100 万）Token 上下文，输入类型覆盖文本、图片、视频，输出为文本；视觉规格方面，单张图片最高 1600 万像素、视频最长 2 小时、单个视频最大 2GB。需要说明的是，官方目前尚未公布参数规模、是否开源等关键指标，网传数值缺乏官方背书，选型时应以官网与模型列表页披露的信息为准。

三、Qwen4-Max大模型功能

从可用功能看，Qwen4-Max 预览版围绕"能调工具、能控过程、能对接业务"三件事展开：

- 函数调用与内置工具：原生支持 Function Calling、联网搜索与内置工具，具备搭建多工具工作流的基础。
- 结构化输出：支持 JSON Object、JSON Schema 等结构化输出，方便把模型结果直接接入业务系统，减少后处理成本。
- 深度思考与推理力度可调：默认开启深度思考模式，可调整推理力度，在精度与速度之间自由取舍。
- 多模态理解：可直接读取页面截图、带图表的文档与视频内容，不必把不同输入拆给不同模型分别处理。
- 接口兼容：兼容 OpenAI Chat Completions、Responses 以及 Anthropic Messages 等接口格式，原有业务代码迁移成本较低。
- 多入口体验：除 API 调用外，还可通过 Qoder、千问办公、千问 App、QwenStudio 等入口第一时间体验。

一个容易踩的坑是输出预算的计法：据官方说明，从这个预览模型开始，max_tokens 与 max_completion_tokens 限制的都是"思考内容 + 最终回答"的总量。如果仍按旧习惯只给最终回答留额度，长推理任务就可能提前截断。

四、Qwen4-Max大模型适用场景

结合官方定位与早期实测反馈，Qwen4-Max 更适合"对结果质量敏感、流程长、步骤多"的任务：

- 复杂编程开发：全栈项目代码生成、仓库级代码审计与重构、前端页面设计、3D 建模脚本、软件自动化流程搭建。
- 多步骤 Agent 智能体：需要多轮工具协同、自动拆分目标的长周期任务，例如科研流水线、财务自动分析、多步骤办公自动化机器人。
- 长文档与混合资料分析：几十万字合同、整本书籍、完整代码库的一次性读取，以及条款比对、风险识别、内容归纳；图文、表格、视频混合资料的联合研判。
- 专业办公与专业软件操作：财报深度解读、法律合同审阅、行业调研报告撰写、专业软件操作自动化等。

不太适合它的场景：高并发、低延迟、成本敏感的简单问答与文案生成。这类任务使用 Qwen4-Flash 或 Qwen4-Plus 更划算——把旗舰模型用在旗舰任务上，才是成本与效果之间的平衡点。

五、Qwen4-Max大模型收费标准

这是本次发布最需要看清的部分：Qwen4-Max 预览版当前仅通过 Token Plan 订阅制开放调用，暂不支持通用按量付费接口。也就是说，想调用它，需要先订阅 Token Plan，再按用量消耗其中的积分（Credits）。Token Plan 采用 Credits 统一计量，一份订阅可在千问系列模型以及多类工具间通用。2026 年 11 月 9 日生效的官方额度调整后，个人版四档如下：

套餐档位 | 官网价 | 每月 Credits | 备注 
---|---|---|---
Lite | 39 元/月 | 20,000 | 新客首购 5 折，19.5 元/月 
Essential | 79 元/月 | 45,000 | 新客首购 5 折，39.5 元/月 
Standard | 139 元/月 | 80,000 | 附赠 Harness 权益 
Pro | 312 元/月 | 200,000 | 附赠 Harness 权益 

团队版按座席计费，双 11 限时价约为：标准座席 150 元/座席/月、高级座席 550 元/座席/月、尊享座席约 1,298—1,398 元/座席/月（各档原价更高），额度按座席发放，并可叠加共享用量包供全团队共用。更多Token Plan活动详情可参考：https://www.aliyun.com/benefit/scene/tokenplan

费用抵扣遵循固定顺序：免费额度 → 资源包 → 节省计划 → 按量付费。订阅额度按月重置、不结转；额度用尽后可购买用量包补足（100 元/个，含 20,000 Credits，最多同时持有 5 个）。此外，Standard 及以上档位附赠 Harness 权益，其中联网搜索、网页解析、图像生成、代码解释器、知识库、沙箱等多项工具能力不消耗 Credits——把"工具活"走 Harness、把 Credits 留给纯模型推理，能明显压低实际成本。

六、Qwen4-Max大模型便宜购买方法

想把成本压到最低，核心是两个动作：先领免费额度把效果验证清楚，再卡住订阅折扣把单价摊薄。

1、先免费试用，把额度用足

阿里云百炼面向新用户的免费额度是行业里比较大方的：完成实名认证、首次开通百炼服务的新用户，可免费领取超 7,000 万 Tokens。活动详情可参考：https://free.aliyun.com/product/ai

它的规则需要记牢：

- 额度分配：每款主流模型分配约 100 万 Tokens，覆盖千问系列对话模型、代码模型与多模态模型，不同模型额度独立计算；完成企业认证的用户，累计可领到 1 亿以上 Tokens。
- 有效期与地域：有效期 90 天，仅限华北 2（北京）地域使用，其他地域无法抵扣。
- 生效方式：不是注册即得，必须在百炼控制台完成服务开通并切换至华北 2（北京）地域，额度才会生效，一般两小时内下发。
- 抵扣范围：仅限实时推理（API 调用或控制台同步对话），不支持批量任务、微调训练与模型部署；主账号与 RAM 子账号共用同一额度池。
- 防超支：某个模型免费额度耗尽时，系统不会自动切换其他模型继续服务，建议开启"用完即停"防护，避免意外产生按量账单。

2、选择使用 Token Plan 订阅方案

先弄清 Token Plan 是什么：它是阿里云百炼推出的按月付费 AI 大模型订阅服务，用统一的 Credits 计量调用额度，一份订阅即可在千问系列模型以及配套工具中通用，不用为每个模型、每个工具单独充值和记账。

为什么用 Token Plan 会更便宜：传统按量付费按 Token 逐条计费，工具一多、模型一多，账单既难预测也难对账；Token Plan 把"单次调用多少钱"变成"一份固定月费能覆盖多少连续消耗"，费用可预算、用量可控制，叠加新客折扣与大促价之后，单位调用成本明显低于按量付费。超出部分还能用用量包（100 元/20,000 Credits）补充，也比溢出后按量计费更省。活动页：https://www.aliyun.com/benefit/scene/tokenplan

当下个人版与团队版优惠价：

- 个人版：新客首购 5 折，Lite 低至 19.5 元/月、Essential 低至 39.5 元/月；Standard 139 元/月、Pro 312 元/月。新客 5 折仅限从未购买过 Token Plan 个人版的账号，同一实名主体限购一份，优惠有效期至 2026 年 11 月 30 日 23:59:59。
- 团队版：按座席购买，标准座席 150 元/座席/月、高级座席 550 元/座席/月、尊享座席约 1,298—1,398 元/座席/月，适合 5 人以上、有多个项目并行、需要把 AI 成本算到部门的团队。

本次最值得关注的折扣组合：Qwen4-Max 预览版首发上线 Token Plan，Token Plan 新客首购低至 5 折；在此基础上，调用 Qwen4 限时 2 折，新用户再叠加 5 折，最低 1 折即可抢先体验 Qwen4。也就是说，一个从没买过 Token Plan 的新账号，可以先用 7,000 万免费 Tokens 验证效果，再以 19.5 元/月的价格订阅 Lite，用极低的成本把预览版跑起来。

不过有三点务必注意：其一，模型调用折扣属于限时安排，到期后回归标准价，长周期项目要按标准价做预算；其二，模型调用折扣与订阅费是两笔账，不要混在一起算；其三，预览版模型标识会在 2026 年 11 月 25 日下线，正式版将以新的模型名发布，接入方要预留迁移和预算调整的空间。把这几条边界写进预算表，优惠才真正省得下来。
