cross_cutting.title: Introducing Clef: Cloudflare's first open-source decision models, now on Workers AI
cross_cutting.description: Cloudflare's first open-source decision models, now on Workers AI ... Meet@cf/cloudflare/clef and @cf/cloudflare/clef-flash, the first models trained by the Cloudflare Workers AI team, available on Workers AI today.
cross_cutting.content:
# Introducing Clef: Cloudflare's first open-source decision models, now on Workers AI
import { TypeScriptExample } from "~/components";

Meet@cf/cloudflare/clef and @cf/cloudflare/clef-flash, the first models trained by the Cloudflare Workers AI team, available on Workers AI today.

Clef is a decision model, in the same family as Typesafe's Jev. Instead of generating text, it reads an input state and a set of typed questions, then returns a probability for every allowed answer. Your agent gets a structured decision it can act on immediately, for example: route the ticket, block the request, or escalate to a human. There is no free-form output to parse and no reasoning tokens to wait for.

Both models are hosted on Workers AI as Clef and Clef-flash. We are also open-sourcing the weights under the Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face: Clef and Clef-flash. Read the launch blog post for the full story, including how we trained them.

We are also launching a reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tuning service to help you tune Clef for your own workloads. Sign up to work with us as a design partner.

## Built for the hot path

Clef is designed to be fast so decisions come back in milliseconds. Across our 43 benchmark runs, we achieved speeds where Clef is 2.5x faster than Jev at the median, and Clef-flash 13x faster.

Latency | Clef | Clef-flash | Jev 
---|---|---|---
Median | 209.3 ms | 38.8 ms | 524.1 ms 
p95 | 238.6 ms | 122.4 ms | 536.0 ms 

Hosting on Workers AI adds to that speed. Requests run on GPUs across Cloudflare's network, running close to your users, so the network round trip stays short. You can put Clef directly in the request path of your agent, then hand off to an LLM on Workers AI to take action.

## Leading the benchmarks

Across 10 decision benchmarks, a Clef model scores highest on 7, ahead of Jev and other open decision models. A few highlights:

Benchmark | Clef | Clef-flash | Jev 
---|---|---|---
BFCL (case exact) | 98.47 | 98.76 | 95.75 
BANKING77 (macro-F1) | 94.20 | 90.93 | 79.74 
CLINC150+OOS (macro-F1) | 97.43 | 66.77 | 89.27 
Home appliances (case exact) | 82.95 | 97.73 | 52.27 

On Typesafe's own workflow evals, Clef beats Jev in 3 of 4 areas: invoice processing, customer service, and security incidents. The full results are on the Hugging Face model card.

## Drop-in compatible with Jev

Model | Size | Best for | Context window 
---|---|---|---
@cf/cloudflare/clef27B | Highest-precision decisions | 64K tokens 
@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash9B | Latency-critical, hot-path decisions | 64K tokens 

Clef follows the System One API, so you can switch an existing Jev integration to Clef by changing the endpoint and model. Ask up to 64 questions per request, in three types:

- noul: A yes/no question. Returns the probability that the answer is yes.
- choice: Pick one option from a set you define. Returns the chosen option, a probability per option, and a confidence value.
- score: Rate against an ordered rubric. Returns a probability-weighted score and a probability per level.

const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/cloudflare/clef", {
	model: "clef",
	state: "Checkout has been failing for every customer for the last hour.",
	questions: {
		urgent: {
			type: "noul",
			instructions: "Is this support request urgent?",
		},
		team: {
			type: "choice",
			instructions: "Which team should handle this request?",
			criteria: {
				billing: "Payments, invoices, and refunds",
				technical: "Outages, errors, and configuration",
				sales: "Plans and upgrades",
			},
		},
	},
});

// response.answers.urgent.noul -> probability the request is urgent
// response.answers.team.choice -> highest-probability team

## What you can build with decision models

- Support triage: Decide whether a ticket is urgent and which team owns it, then route it without a human in the loop.
- Threat intelligence: Classify a website by category. Paired with Browser Run, Clef fetched, rendered, and classified a domain in 2.2 seconds, compared to 4.7 seconds forgpt-oss-120b in the same workflow.
- Trust and safety: Score user submissions against your own policy rubric and act on the probability.
- Agent guardrails: Let an agent check "should I take this action?" in tens of milliseconds before calling a tool.
- Visual classification: Pass up to four images alongside the state. Unlike text-only decision models, Clef has a vision encoder.

## Get started

Use Clef through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()) or the REST API at /ai/run. You can also use AI Gateway with these endpoints.

For more information, refer to the Clef model page, the Clef-flash model page, and pricing.

cross_cutting.title: Open Source AI — November 12, 2026 — Lucien Engelen
cross_cutting.description: A Chinese delivery company released a 1.6-trillion-parameter model that anyone may use commercially, and Tether published a model under one billion parameters built to run on a device. ... Meituan published the weights on November 9 on Hugging Face, permitting commercial use, modification and redistribution.
cross_cutting.content:
# Open Source AI — November 12, 2026

CloudZero's telemetry from 32 organizations puts the average price paid per million inference tokens at $0.69 in October, down 20% in a month and 34% since July (the thesis says this number should rise).

## Hook of the Day

CloudZero's telemetry from 32 organizations puts the average price paid per million inference tokens at $0.69 in October, down 20% in a month and 34% since July (the thesis says this number should rise).

## In Plain English

A Chinese delivery company released a 1.6-trillion-parameter model that anyone may use commercially, and Tether published a model under one billion parameters built to run on a device. Meanwhile the price companies actually pay per token keeps falling, and analysts doubt that all the announced AI data centers will get built.

## Section A: Open-Weight Models

Meituan's LongCat-2.5 is a trillion-scale MIT-licensed release, and its own numbers still show a gap to Claude Opus 5 on the harder terminal benchmark. MBZUAI adds an Apache 2.0 world model, so the open side now covers physical simulation as well as text.

### Meituan releases LongCat-2.5 weights under an MIT license

Meituan published the weights on November 9 on Hugging Face, permitting commercial use, modification and redistribution. It is a mixture-of-experts model with about 1.6 trillion total parameters and roughly 48 billion active per token (Hugging Face metadata shows 1.8 trillion, which Silicon Report could not reconcile with the model card). Meituan reports 88.4 on Terminal Bench v2.1 against 70.8 for LongCat 2.0, but 38.5 on Terminal Bench v4.0 against 53.9 for Claude Opus 5 in its own comparison. Its API costs $0.30 per million input tokens and $1.20 per million output tokens (promotional). All benchmarks are vendor-reported.

Silicon Report · Open-weight release · November 10, 2026

### MBZUAI's IFM releases PAN 2, an open 29B world model

The Institute of Foundation Models at MBZUAI released PAN 2 under Apache 2.0. It pairs an LLM planner with a 29-billion-parameter diffusion transformer and simulates up to 20 seconds of action outcomes as video. The MarkTechPost page would not open, so this rests on the feed summary of the article only.

MarkTechPost · Open-weight release · November 11, 2026

## Section B: Infrastructure & Token Economics

Today's data runs against the first leg of the thesis: effective token prices fell, and Anthropic describes software gains that cut the compute it needs. The supply side is the open question, since an analyst says many announced data centers will never be built.

### CloudZero: average inference price fell to $0.69 per million tokens in October

CloudZero reports an average effective price of $0.69 per million tokens in October, from $0.86 in September and $1.03 in July (22 to 32 organizations per month, so the panel changes). The figure reflects cache hits and usage mix, not list prices. Median AI spend growth per company slowed to 1.8% in October, against 13.3% in July, and the share of companies spending at least a quarter of their cloud budget on AI reached 9.8%. The price series and the spend series come from different company groups, as the article itself notes.

CloudZero (Keith MacKenzie) · Token economics · November 10, 2026

### Anthropic's IPO roadshow: one model family on four chip families

In the roadshow video, co-founder Tom Brown says Anthropic trains and serves Claude on AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, Nvidia GPUs and AMD GPUs. He says the Mythos model ported Claude to AMD in three days with almost no human intervention, and he describes "compute multipliers": a 4x multiplier means 25 units of compute do the work of 100. Simon Willison's post, built on his own MacWhisper transcript, contains no margin, revenue or capex figures.

Simon Willison's Weblog · Infrastructure · November 11, 2026

### Analyst: many announced AI data centers will not get built

On TechCrunch's Equity podcast, Brent Nelson of Ascend Analytics says the pipeline of announced AI data centers is "wildly inflated" and that not every proposed one will be built, citing permitting delays and electricity supply. Only show notes were available, no transcript. DatacenterDynamics separately reports a 10-year data center moratorium in Ottawa, Kansas, after the hyperscale project that sparked protests had already been cancelled (its page would not open, so this is the feed summary only).

TechCrunch Equity · Infrastructure · November 11, 2026

## Section C: On-Prem & On-Device Shift

One item today, and a small one: a sub-billion-parameter model aimed at running on a personal device. It shows how much tool-calling ability now fits in a file small enough for a laptop or phone, though the authors give no device figures.

### Tether's QVAC releases BotPsy-0.8B, an on-device agent model

Tether AI Research built BotPsy-0.8B on Qwen3.5-0.8B for function calling, with GGUF builds in bf16, Q8 and Q4. The authors report an average of 45.0 across tool-use tests against 38.8 for Qwen3.5-2B-Think, a model 2.5 times its size, and BFCL v4 of 44.0 against 37.7. The larger model still leads on Claw-Eval (48.9 against 46.5) and on knowledge tests such as GPQA Diamond. Benchmarks are self-reported, the Apache 2.0 license is for research and educational use and is worded in the future tense, and the post gives no RAM or speed figures.

Hugging Face blog (QVAC) · On-device model · November 11, 2026

## The Apple Angle

Some commentators argue that Apple, not Nvidia, is best placed for the shift to local inference. The Substack piece behind this view describes a Mac Studio with 512GB of unified memory, bought for about $9,500, that holds very large open-weight models which would otherwise need five or six Nvidia RTX Pro 6000 cards (about $60,000 to $75,000, roughly ten times the power draw). Its logic: as capable open-weight models keep shipping, the bottleneck moves from who has the best model to who has affordable hardware to run it. The counterpoint is that a Mac Studio suits one user with a lot of memory, while datacenter GPU clusters serve many users at once. Mac Studio memory configurations have changed since that article was written, so check Apple's current options before relying on the 512GB figure.

Limited Edition Jonathan (Substack) · Perspective

## Why This Matters

The $0.69 average price and Anthropic's compute multipliers both point to cheaper tokens today, which weakens the "prices will rise" leg until the build-out shortfall the analyst describes shows up in supply. LongCat-2.5 and BotPsy show open weights at both ends of the size range, with the largest model still trailing Opus 5 on the hardest test.

### Book Lucien for your next event

Keynotes, masterclasses, panels and board-room sessions.

cross_cutting.title: 亚马逊 SageMaker JumpStart 新增 Ornith-1.0-9B 和 Ornith-1.0-35B 模型
cross_cutting.description: 亚马逊 SageMaker JumpStart 于 2026 年 11 月 11 日新增了 DeepReinforce AI 的 Ornith-1.0-9B 和 Ornith-1.0-35B AI 智能体编程模型，扩展了 AWS 基础模型组合 ... 据 2026 年 11 月 11 日发布的一则动态，DeepReinforce AI 的 Ornith-1.0-9B 和 Ornith-1.0-35B 模型现已在 Amazon SageMaker JumpStart 上提供。
cross_cutting.content:
关键要点

亚马逊 SageMaker JumpStart 于 2026 年 11 月 11 日新增了 DeepReinforce AI 的 Ornith-1.0-9B 和 Ornith-1.0-35B AI 智能体编程模型，扩展了 AWS 基础模型组合。

Ornith-1.0-9B 在单张 GPU 上支持 25.6 万个词元的上下文窗口，而 Ornith-1.0-35B 采用混合专家架构，可部署在配备 24GB 显存的消费级 GPU 上。

两款 Ornith 1.0 模型在 Terminal-Bench 2.1、SWE-Bench、NL2Repo 和 OpenClaw 基准测试中的编程表现均达到最先进水平，并采用 MIT 许可证。

据 2026 年 11 月 11 日发布的一则动态，DeepReinforce AI 的 Ornith-1.0-9B 和 Ornith-1.0-35B 模型现已在 Amazon SageMaker JumpStart 上提供。这一上线扩充了面向 AWS 客户提供的基础模型组合。这两款模型均属于 Ornith 1.0 系列，是基于 MIT 许可发布的开源、能够自行构建脚手架的智能体编程模型；在 Terminal-Bench 2.1、SWE-Bench、NL2Repo 和 OpenClaw 等编程基准测试中，它们的表现达到同等规模开源模型中的最先进水平。

Ornith-1.0-9B 将智能体编程带到单 GPU 部署场景

Ornith-1.0-9B 是一款轻量级的 90 亿参数稠密模型，基于 Qwen 3.5 9B 进行后训练，旨在实现高效的单 GPU 部署。该模型具有 25.6 万 token 的上下文窗口和 32 个解码器层。来源称，该模型非常适合个人开发者和小型团队在单 GPU 上运行智能体编程工作流，包括使用消费级硬件的笔记本电脑。其自我改进训练框架使用强化学习联合优化脚手架生成和解决方案推理；来源称，这使模型能够发现更优的搜索路径并生成质量更高的代码解决方案。

Ornith-1.0-35B 将混合专家架构与 24GB 消费级 GPU 相结合

Ornith-1.0-35B 是一款 350 亿参数的混合专家（MoE）模型，基于 Qwen 3.5 进行后训练。来源称，该模型在保持可部署于单张 24GB 消费级 GPU 上的同时，提供更强的智能体编程性能。与 9B 模型一样，它使用强化学习联合优化用于编程任务的脚手架生成和由此产生的解决方案推理，从而发现更优的代码路径。据来源介绍，其 MoE 架构仅针对每个 token 激活部分参数，在生产级智能体编程工作负载中兼顾质量与效率。

SageMaker JumpStart 支持通过控制台和 SDK 部署两款模型

据来源介绍，客户只需点击几下，即可部署这些模型以满足特定的 AI 使用场景。要开始使用，用户可以前往 SageMaker 控制台中的 SageMaker JumpStart 模型目录，也可以使用 SageMaker Python SDK 将模型部署到自己的 AWS 账户。来源建议读者参阅 Amazon SageMaker JumpStart 文档，了解在 SageMaker JumpStart 中部署和使用基础模型的更多信息。

Ornith 1.0 模型规格与部署详情

Ornith-1.0-9B：90 亿参数稠密模型，基于 Qwen 3.5 9B 进行后训练，具有 25.6 万 token 的上下文窗口和 32 个解码器层

Ornith-1.0-35B：350 亿参数混合专家模型，基于 Qwen 3.5 进行后训练，可部署于单张 24GB 消费级 GPU

许可：MIT 许可，开源

提及的编程基准测试：Terminal-Bench 2.1、SWE-Bench、NL2Repo 和 OpenClaw

两款模型均使用强化学习联合优化脚手架生成和解决方案推理

部署方式：SageMaker 控制台中的 SageMaker JumpStart 模型目录，或 SageMaker Python SDK

哪些模型现已在 Amazon SageMaker JumpStart 上提供？

DeepReinforce AI 的 Ornith-1.0-9B 和 Ornith-1.0-35B 模型现已在 Amazon SageMaker JumpStart 上提供。两款模型均属于 Ornith 1.0 系列，是基于 MIT 许可发布的开源、能够自行构建脚手架的智能体编程模型。

部署 Ornith-1.0-35B 模型需要什么硬件？

来源称，Ornith-1.0-35B 可部署于单张 24GB 消费级 GPU。它是一款基于 Qwen 3.5 进行后训练的 350 亿参数混合专家模型。

客户如何在 SageMaker JumpStart 上部署 Ornith 1.0 模型？

客户前往 SageMaker 控制台中的 SageMaker JumpStart 模型目录，只需点击几下即可部署这些模型。或者，也可以使用 SageMaker Python SDK 将模型部署到自己的 AWS 账户。

cross_cutting.description: Vercel finds a typical AI model peaks within four weeks of its launch ... Illustrating the trend, Vercel reports that Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 was the top model by spend in its first full month, following its launch on September 22, 2026.
cross_cutting.content:
## 'Teams are moving to new models almost as fast as labs release them': Vercel data reveals AI models now have a half-life of just six weeks — with most most AI traffic running on models less than two months old

techradar.com35min

## AI now has a half-life

- Vercel finds a typical AI model peaks within four weeks of its launch
- Anthropic is outperforming OpenAI in attracting new teams of users
- Users are keen to stay ahead of the curve, with no show of loyalty

The time spent with a new AI model is decreasing, with teams using paid AI services sticking with a new model for an average of four weeks. At that point, they switch to another new model, aiming to keep their AI code development or agents competitive.

Vercel’s AI Gateway Production Index report for November 2026 claims this trend indicates that AI models effectively have a half-life of around six weeks. At that point, attention and use of the model decreases as teams and developers proceed to switch to the latest shiny alternative.

Illustrating the trend, Vercel reports that Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 was the top model by spend in its first full month, following its launch on September 22, 2026.

## The AI half-life

While the concept of an AI model having a half-life may initially seem outlandish, it actually makes perfect sense.

Vercel’s analysis of token transactions via its gateway shows that teams adopt new models within days of them being launched. Assuming the use of a code editor or tool wrapper, pointing a development environment to a new model can be achieved relatively painlessly.
 You may like 
Vercel’s data breaks down the adoption rate into 00-14 days, 15-30 days, and 31-60 days, and highlights a trend towards increased early adoption from June 2026 onward. By September, almost 17% were using models that had been available for under two weeks.

But older models are retained to some degree, but these are typically relying on less usage and, consequently, token spend.

So, with new models being released relatively regularly by competing AI platforms, and with easy model switching essentially baked into developers environments, they’re being used with an initial intensity that wanes when the next model launches. Hence Vercel’s determination that models “have a half-life of about six weeks.”

## Video models

Vercel also determined that the top model by spend in its first full month in October was Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5, drawing just over 14% in spend.

Meanwhile, the most widely used paid models are dominated by Anthropic. Sonnet 5.5 (26%), Haiku 5.5 (22%), Haiku 4.5 (20%), and Opus 5.5 (18%) are the most widely-used, although there is duplication, with many team apparently relying on multiple models.

Significantly, image and video generation was also prominent, with more spend and adoption than in previous months. One in six AI development teams are now using a video model, up from 10% in previous months. This is where OpenAI had a rare chance to shine in Vercel's report, with its GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst leading in image generation model spend during October.

cross_cutting.content:
# Vercel Data Puts AI Model Half-Life at Just Six Weeks

Vercel's November 2026 AI Gateway report finds AI models have a six-week half-life as developer teams switch labs rapidly and Opus 5.5 leads spend.

Engineering teams using paid AI services stick with a newly adopted model for an average of four weeks before moving on, establishing an effective AI model half-life of roughly six weeks, according to Vercel's November 2026 AI Gateway Production Index. Analyzing more than 100 trillion monthly tokens routed through October 2026, authors Amelia Charles and Harpreet Arora found that over half of all language-model requests targeted releases under 60 days old—a share that never topped 30% before September.

Because code editors, tool wrappers, and unified gateways let developers repoint an environment with minimal effort, teams adopt new releases within days. Vercel's cohort breakdown across 0–14, 15–30, and 31–60 days shows early adoption climbing steadily since June 2026; by September, nearly 17% (about one in six) of language-model requests ran on models under two weeks old.

Across model families, a new version arrives every 61 days at the median and peaks within four weeks. Four weeks past peak, three in four teams have moved their primary traffic elsewhere whether or not a direct successor shipped. Half of paid teams processing at least 10 million monthly tokens changed their top model in October, with 80% choosing a newer release and 60% switching labs. Older models linger only in minor roles: 70% of those high-volume teams still called a 10-month-old model in October, but for less than 3% of typical token volume.

## How Paid Models Compare Under a Six-Week AI Model Half-Life

Anthropic held four of the six widest-reach slots on Vercel's gateway in October. Claude Opus 5.5, launched September 22, 2026, led all models in dollar spend during its first full month at just over 14% (about one in seven dollars). Reach figures overlap because multi-model stacks dominate: the top 1% of spenders run a median of 29 models versus one for the bottom tenth.

Overall lab reach across paid teams is now virtually tied at 55% for OpenAI and 54% for Anthropic, compared with 70% versus 48% last December. New paid teams picked Anthropic nearly two to one over OpenAI in October—and 42.7% to 24.0% across recent months, ahead of Google (16.5%) and DeepSeek (6.6%). Anthropic still captures roughly 32% of total gateway spend (down half since December), while OpenAI rose by two-thirds to nearly 15%. Over 90% of top-percentile spenders pay both labs.

## Decision, Image, and Voice Workloads Split the Stack

- Decision models hit 26% of requests for 0.53% of spend: Added in mid-September across 15 models from eight vendors, classifiers cost roughly one-seventieth per request of a language model. Led by TypeSafe AI's Jev decision engine, nearly a third of paid teams—and 70% above 10 billion monthly tokens—used one in October, just ahead of Google's Gemini Decision 1 API launch.
- Video and image spend climbs: One in six AI development teams among top spenders used a video model in October, up from 10% in July, led in spend by ByteDance's Seedance 2.5 ahead of Google Veo 3.1 and Kuaishou Kling 3.0. OpenAI's GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst topped image generation spend.
- Modular voice grows 2.6x: Voice adoption rose 161% since July to 11% of paid teams, with a quarter now assembling separate speech-to-text (8.0%) and text-to-speech (5.2%) endpoints around their chosen language model.

## Why It Matters: Zero Switching Costs Erode Model Moats

Rapid model rotation clarifies why token volumes keep surging even as US corporate AI spending growth cooled to 1.65% in October. Unified gateways and automated code routers let builders route classification to sub-cent decision models while swapping frontier checkpoints the week a stronger version lands.

One caveat applies: Vercel estimates spend at list prices across agile gateway users, whereas enterprises on multi-year cloud contracts likely switch slower. Even so, labs must now re-earn developer traffic every two months. Watch December's index to see whether Google's Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini Decision 1 dent Anthropic's 5.5 lead.

cross_cutting.content:
# Databricks unveils new version of AI agent Genie

## AI Summary Databricks on Nov. 11 unveiled a new version of its AI agent, Genie. TechCrunch reported that the updated tool can support multi-step work that takes a long time. Databricks built an ontology to provide Genie with context from information customers store on the platform. CEO Ali Ghodsi showed his own agent with recent conversations and charts, and said he uses it to surface issues hard to hear at the top.

- Writer Chi-gyu Hwang
- published 2026-11-12 14:52:09
- updated 2026-11-12 14:53:09

Databricks said on Nov. 11 it has unveiled a new version of its AI agent, Genie.

TechCrunch reported that Genie supports multi-step tasks that take a long time to complete.

Databricks also built an ontology to provide Genie with context from information customers store on the Databricks platform.

The company said executives can assign Genie a range of tasks and it can finish them without human supervision.

Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi (알리 고드시) opened the agent he actually uses instead of giving a product demo, showing recent conversations and charts.

Genie analysed low-scoring items in an employee satisfaction survey. It also supported evaluating and filtering improvement proposals from some executives. It summarised how a large sales proposal to a potential customer failed. The summary included features the customer demanded as purchase conditions. TechCrunch reported that Genie also reviewed past broadcasts featuring Ghodsi and generated expected questions for a podcast interview.

Ghodsi said he uses Genie to find things that are hard to hear from the CEO seat. He described it as a channel for hearing unvarnished accounts of what is not going well at the company.

At a small startup, a CEO knows all employees and staff can relay bad news immediately, but Databricks has 12,000 employees. At that scale, failures in the sales field are difficult to reach the CEO.

Ghodsi said, "There are many companies with more than 150 employees," and added, "Many people can get value from Genie."

Databricks is pitching Genie as an always-on agent for executives. Ghodsi said he also uses Genie in his personal life instead of OpenClaw, Instinct and Muse, which he said have questionable security. He said Genie can play the role in business that AI, agents and harnesses play for programmers.

On concerns that agents could increase corporate AI costs, he said, "You can control it with Unity Gateway," adding, "Companies can set usage limits with this product and switch to cheaper open-weight models."

cross_cutting.title: Databricks expands Genie into an always-on AI agent for enterprise workflows
cross_cutting.description: Databricks expands Genie into an always-on AI agent for enterprise workflows Databricks has announced a new version of its Genie platform, turning the enterprise AI assistant into an always-on agent designed to manage tasks autonomously and support decision-making across business functions.
cross_cutting.content:
# Databricks expands Genie into an always-on AI agent for enterprise workflows

Databricks has announced a new version of its Genie platform, turning the enterprise AI assistant into an always-on agent designed to manage tasks autonomously and support decision-making across business functions.

The second-generation Genie can take ownership of tasks assigned by employees, track their progress, delegate work to smaller AI agents and follow up when additional information is required. It can also notify users when a decision or intervention is needed through a new priority inbox and email alerts.

The announcement reflects a broader shift in enterprise AI adoption, as businesses look beyond tools that answer questions towards systems that can manage workflows and carry out tasks across multiple applications. However, such systems need access to relevant business information and must operate within an organisation’s existing security and governance policies.

Databricks said the new Genie is designed to address these requirements through its Genie Ontology, which maintains an understanding of how a company operates, including its data, business definitions, people and processes.

Genie moves from answering queries to managing tasks

The updated Genie can operate in the background using its own computing resources. Employees can assign it a goal and define the boundaries within which it can work. It then manages the task and contacts the user when it requires additional information or a decision.

For instance, a marketing team could ask Genie to monitor generative engine optimisation (GEO) performance and suggest relevant content. Customer success teams could use it to track changes in customer usage patterns and alert account managers when activity shifts. Executives could also ask it to monitor revenue trends and customer feature requests before preparing regular business updates.

The platform can delegate work to multiple sub-agents, allowing different parts of a task to be handled in parallel. A new priority inbox is intended to bring decisions and pending actions to the user’s attention, while email alerts provide updates when users are away from the application.

Databricks CEO and co-founder Ali Ghodsi said Genie had made him more productive by keeping track of emails, preparing him for meetings and working in the background. He attributed this capability to the platform’s understanding of company-specific information, including business definitions, official metrics and access permissions.

Genie Ontology provides business context to AI agents

A key part of the announcement is Genie Ontology, which Databricks describes as an agentic ontology for enterprise AI.

In simple terms, an ontology helps an AI system understand how information relates to a business. It can provide context about what particular metrics mean, how business processes work, which teams are responsible for them and how different pieces of information are connected.

This is important because enterprise information is often spread across different systems and departments. The same business term may also have different meanings across teams. Without this context, an AI agent may retrieve information but misunderstand its relevance or provide an answer that does not reflect how the organisation operates.

Databricks said Genie Ontology maintains this business context as the organisation changes. It is designed to help Genie interpret both structured data, such as tables and metrics, and unstructured information, such as documents and other business content.

The company is also introducing Ontology Manager, a new interface through which teams can manage and govern business context. It will provide recommendations to identify frequently used concepts that may need further refinement.

Genie Search expands access to enterprise information

Alongside the updated agent, Databricks is expanding Genie Search to help employees and AI agents find information across enterprise data systems and business applications.

The search capability is designed to work across the Databricks lakehouse and external platforms such as Google Drive, Jira and Confluence. Databricks said it now supports more than 100 connectors, offering different ways to access information. These include bringing data into the lakehouse, indexing information where it is stored or querying applications through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

The aim is to allow AI agents to search across structured and unstructured information without having to check each application separately. By using Genie Ontology, the search system can also interpret information in the context of business definitions and processes, rather than simply returning documents that match a query.

Databricks said the system follows existing access permissions and allows teams to inspect the sources behind the information retrieved. This is particularly relevant for enterprises where employees and AI agents may have different levels of access to business data.

Governance remains central to autonomous AI deployment

As AI agents gain the ability to access enterprise applications and perform tasks, organisations need to ensure that their actions remain within defined security boundaries.

Databricks said Genie operates within a company’s existing environment and is governed by Unity Catalog and Unity Gateway. Unity Catalog manages permissions and access to enterprise data, while Unity Gateway provides controls for AI model and tool usage, including approval rules and budgets.

The company said every action taken by Genie remains subject to these controls and is auditable. This is intended to allow enterprises to introduce autonomous workflows without creating a separate set of permissions and governance systems for the agent.

The announcement also includes capabilities to generate data-driven presentations, dashboards and interactive reports that remain connected to governed data. Genie Agents will additionally be able to work with documents such as PDFs, contracts and presentations stored in Unity Catalog volumes.

Databricks also highlighted customer use cases. HelloFresh said its use of Genie to analyse performance signals had improved programme-level advertising returns and reduced the time taken to identify effective advertisements on Meta by 75%. The company also cited adoption by Headspace, which said governed business definitions had helped expand access to self-service analytics.

cross_cutting.content:
# 新版Genie智能体上线：Databricks CEO称其能揭示未经修饰的真相

Databricks更新AI代理Genie，支持多步骤自主任务处理，借助本体论架构理解客户数据上下文。CEO Ali Ghodsi公开展示其内部使用场景，包括员工满意度分析、销售复盘与播客备稿，并称可通过Unity Gateway控制使用成本。

Databricks周三发布了其AI智能体Genie的更新版本，该版本现在能够执行需要长时间才能完成的多步骤任务。公司通过构建的一套本体论（ontology）来实现这一点，为Genie提供从客户存储在Databricks平台上的信息中获取所需的上下文。

据该公司介绍，企业管理者现在可以为该智能体分配各种各样的任务，它将在无人监督的情况下完成这些任务。为了证明这一点，Databricks首席执行官阿里·戈德西（Ali Ghodsi）向笔者展示了他在公司内部如何使用该产品。他没有做产品演示，而是直接打开了自己正在使用的智能体，并带笔者浏览了他最近的对话记录和图表。

他展示了该智能体如何分析一份员工满意度调查中公司表现不佳的部分，以及它如何帮助他评估（并剔除）一些高管针对这些低分项提出的改进建议。他还展示了该智能体如何总结一次进展不顺利的重要销售推介，包括潜在客户在表示购买之前所提出的必要功能需求。

该智能体还通过回顾他以往的播客访谈经历，为他准备了一次播客采访，并预测了可能被问到的问题。在我们交谈的过程中，他甚至让智能体告诉他该如何回答我的问题。（而且它给出的建议还不错。）

有趣的地方在于，戈德西正在利用Genie去发现那些作为公司大老板已经很难直接听到的信息。这成为了他了解公司内部哪些环节运转不畅、需要加以处理的真实信息来源，而这些信息往往未经修饰。

“你听说过邓巴数字吗？这个神奇的数字是150，”在笔者指出这一点时，戈德西说道。这一概念以英国人类学家罗宾·邓巴（Robin Dunbar）命名，理论上是人类能够维持稳定关系的最大人数。在一家小型初创公司里，CEO认识每一个人，与他们都有直接联系，员工也会感到安全，愿意向他直言不讳地反映负面信息。

而在拥有1.2万名员工的公司里，戈德西坦言自己无法认识所有人。在这种规模下，一名销售人员不太可能向CEO坦白一次失败的销售电话。一名人力资源经理也不太可能承认自己提出的提升员工满意度的方案可能会失败。

“任何拥有超过150名员工的组织——这其实是很多公司——其中很多人都可以从这类产品中获益，”他在谈到AI智能体这一整体概念，以及具体谈到其产品Genie时这样说道。

戈德西自己使用Genie的做法（通常被称为“自己吃自己的狗粮”，源自“eating your own dogfood”这一说法）正是Databricks现在将其定位为面向企业领导者的常驻智能体的原因之一。他表示，自己在个人生活中也会使用它，而不是选择一些存在安全隐患的替代产品，比如OpenClaw、Instinct或Muse。

他认为，Genie能够为企业业务侧带来的变革，就如同AI、智能体以及“工具外壳”（harness，即包裹在AI模型周围、使其能够使用各种工具的软件）为程序员带来的变革一样。至于智能体可能推高企业AI使用成本的风险，戈德西也给出了答案。他表示，企业可以通过Databricks的Unity Gateway产品来控制成本，该产品允许公司设置使用限额，并切换至成本更低的开放权重模型。

cross_cutting.description: In 2026 it usually means the product isn’t ready to charge for. ... In 2026, Launching Free Usually Means You Can’t Charge for It Yet The standard advice is to launch AI free, get adoption, learn how customers use it, then add pricing. Figma roughly did that.
cross_cutting.content:
# A Great B2B Agent Doubles Your ACV. Most AI Features Don’t Move It at All.

This week one of our portfolio companies launched its first real agent. It’s a vertical software company at about $30M ARR, growing well, with a loyal base and a sales-led motion.

The agent doubles ACV. There’s no free version. In the first week, 3% of the customer base bought it.

I think that’s what a great agent in B2B looks like: customers pay twice as much in the first week because the value is obvious.

I now invest by this rule. I won’t back an agentic B2B company unless it unlocks budget beyond the software budget, and the proof is deal sizes at least 2x what the pre-AI competitors get. Most companies shipping AI right now don’t clear that bar.

Top takeaways:

- A real agent does a job a human used to do. Customers pay for it out of labor budget, which is why it can double ACV.
- AI features that make the existing workflow a bit better don’t move ACV, so vendors meter them with credits on top of seats. Customers experience that as a price increase.
- “Launch free, monetize later” was a reasonable hedge in 2024. In 2026 it usually means the product isn’t ready to charge for.
- If you can’t double ACV, adoption stalls, or customers resent the bill, fix the agent before you touch the pricing.

## 1. An Agent That Doubles ACV Gets Paid From the Labor Budget

Software budgets are capped. Every CIO I talk to is consolidating vendors and cutting existing lines to fund AI. An agent that competes for the software budget is fighting for a shrinking pool, often against its own seat line.

An agent that does real work gets paid from a different budget: the person who used to do that work, the agency, the contractor, or the task that never got done because nobody had time.

That’s how this company can double ACV without pushback. Customers compare the agent to the hours it replaces, and against that number, 2x the subscription is cheap.

It’s also why 3% adoption in week one matters. With a sales-led motion and some onboarding, the whole base was never going to switch in seven days. But 3% of a loyal base paying double in the first week, with no discount and no trial, shows the value was clear before anyone had used it for a month.

## 2. 10K Co-Sold a Six-Figure Deal, and Our Sponsor Renewals Went From the 20s to the 70s

I believe this partly because we’re seeing it at SaaStr.

10K, our AI VP of Marketing, has been running for 11 months. On a six-figure Base44 / Wix deal, it built the decks, priced the custom work, flagged the procurement terms, moved the deal to Commit in Salesforce, and filled out the vendor paperwork. It co-sold the deal alongside me and Amelia.

Renewal rates for our $100K+ sponsors went from the 20s to the 70s this year. 10K says it only deserves credit for “operational support.” Either way, that’s what agent-level value looks like from the buyer’s side. If someone sold me 10K as a product, I’d pay several times what we pay for any single tool in our stack, because I’d be comparing it to the humans we didn’t hire.

Very few vendors selling us AI today are in that category. Most are selling a slightly better version of what we already had.

## 3. HubSpot Tripled a Small Team’s Bill With Credits

When the AI doesn’t do a job on its own, vendors can’t charge 2x, so they meter it.

HubSpot’s new model is this fall’s best-known case. Amelia priced it for a three-person marketing team with 10,000 contacts, a weekly newsletter and about 20,000 workflow actions a month. The old bill was about $1,300 a month. The new bill is about $3,700, mostly credits for workflow actions that used to be unlimited. A newsletter send costs the same credit as an outbound sequence. One HubSpot customer we know called to say the newsletter was moving elsewhere, and got a discount.

The bill tripled, and the customer got no new capability.

Compare the CRM-focused agents in our network: Monaco, Lightfield and Attio. They’re closing much larger deals than in the Pipedrive era because they take over real work. If an agent puts four meetings on your calendar the first week you turn it on, nobody argues about the price.

When customers complain about the bill, the agent usually isn’t doing enough. When they thank you for it, you can charge more.

## 4. Keep the Seat as the Seat. Sell the Agent as Its Own Line.

Products sold per seat should mostly stay per seat. Customers like predictable seat pricing and dislike surprise charges on top of it. Products that were always transactional, close to revenue or data usage like Stripe or Databricks, can be usage-based, and customers accept that.

Trouble starts when vendors want the economics of variable pricing without agent-level value, so they add per-action fees on top of an $80 or $400 seat. The base sees that as a price increase, because it is one.

The companies doing this well keep the seat price where it is and sell the agent as a separate SKU, priced by the job it does. That’s the path to 2x.

## 5. Salesforce Charges a 60-80% Premium, Box 20-40%, and Podium Built $100M in Agent ARR

The incumbents show the range.

Salesforce charges a 60-80% premium for its premium AI editions. As of last quarter, only about 5% of sales and service knowledge workers were on them. Benioff said it directly: “Most of them have not started their AI transformations yet.” The premium exists, and most of the base hasn’t decided it’s worth paying.

Box repackaged around AI with Enterprise Advanced at a 20-40% price premium. It reached about 10% of revenue in under two years, and billings growth picked up before revenue did. That’s a real upgrade path. It’s 20-40% because the product is a better version of the same job.

Podium built $100M in AI agent ARR in under 24 months selling to home services businesses. The agent answers the phone, books the job and follows up, work customers used to pay people to do.

Improving a workflow got Box to 20-40%. Podium’s agent does the work itself, and that’s what supports 2x.

## 6. In 2026, Launching Free Usually Means You Can’t Charge for It Yet

The standard advice is to launch AI free, get adoption, learn how customers use it, then add pricing. Figma roughly did that. At over $1B in revenue and about 92% gross margins, it launched AI free, added credits without charging, then started charging. Ulrik Lehrskov-Schmidt of Willingness to Pay, who joined us on The Agents this week, makes a good case that this captured value the seat model had been missing.

I’m more skeptical. Figma Make was uncompetitive with Replit, Lovable and v0 for a long time, and I think launching free was partly cover for a product the team didn’t think it could charge for. Canva was worse off. It was so worried about token costs eating an 80% gross margin that it never shipped anything competitive enough to charge for. Then the models got better, Gamma and Higgsfield took the use cases, and Canva restructured 22% of the company this month.

I’d make the team charge for it on day one, at the same price as the AI-native leaders or higher. If your own loyal base won’t buy it, you find out in one week instead of four quarters.

There’s one fair exception. Ulrik had a UK client at about $30M that launched its first agent with credits from day one, and adoption stalled. Now they can’t tell whether the product or the pricing failed. If you don’t yet know what the product should do, launch without a paywall to find out, and be honest internally that you’re still in product discovery.

## 7. Five Things a 2x Agent Does

From building our own agents and selling into a base of 400,000 B2B execs, the agents that earn 2x have five traits in common:

- They finish the job. The output is a closed deal, a booked meeting, a resolved ticket or a filed form, with no human needed to finish it.
- They use your data. 10K is valuable because it can see 13 years of invoices, every call note and every sponsor’s results. A horizontal LLM can’t.
- They act without being asked. The agent notices the renewal, flags the upsell and chases the collection. If a human has to start it every time, it’s a feature.
- The buyer can see the result. If customers have to dig through dashboards to find the value, they won’t pay 2x. The agent should show what it did and what it was worth.
- They have guardrails. Our agents need approval for every write to Salesforce. An agent that touches real systems needs permissions and approvals built into the product.

An agent that does all five can charge 2x.

## 8. Three Numbers to Track After Week One

Week one tells you whether customers will pay. Three numbers tell you whether the agent holds up:

- Attach rate at 90 days. Week-one buyers are your most motivated customers. What matters is whether the next cohort, the one that has to be sold, follows them.
- Renewal on the agent line. If it’s the first thing cut at renewal, it was a nice-to-have.
- Core-product retention for agent customers versus everyone else. A real agent makes the whole account stickier, because it’s doing work the customer can’t easily take back in-house.

If all three hold, you’ve doubled the value of the accounts that bought it.

## The Question for Your 2027 Plan

Ask your product team which agent, shipping in the next two quarters, you can charge existing customers 50-100% more for, starting in week one.

If the answer is none, more credits and a higher seat price won’t close the gap. Your most loyal customers will tell you first, usually by calling to say they’re moving something elsewhere.

The company in our portfolio answered that question this week. 3% of its base paid double before the first month was out.

MulmoClaude is an open-source home on your own computer where you grow a personal AI assistant — it builds the apps you ask for in plain conversation (no code), remembers everything in a wiki and in those apps' own data...
cross_cutting.content:
# MulmoClaude — Product Hunt Launch Strategy (v2 — "The Assistant You Nurture")

Canonical launch plan. This file is the single source of truth for the Product Hunt launch. It supersedes the Collections-centered v1 of this file (June 2026, in git history) — the positioning has changed, not just the date. Source of truth for the vision:
../mulmo-p/mulmoclaude/vision/the-assistant-you-nurture_ja.txt. The center is no longer a mechanism (Collections / "AI-native database"); it is a relationship: an AI assistant that knows everything about you cannot be bought — the only way to get one is to grow it yourself, and MulmoClaude is the field you grow it in. Collections, the wiki, the scheduler, and the bridges are now how the nurturing happens — evidence, not the headline. The "AI-native database" category bet and the Karpathy/DSL-as-harness lead are retired from PH surfaces (the harness thesis survives for HN comments and the blog only). The HN launch already ran with little traction (plans/done/launch-hn.md); PH stands alone.
Owner: Satoshi (strategy + maker post), Engineering (demo assets + activation path), Community (day-of ops) Target launch: Tuesday, August 4, 2026 — 12:01 AM PT kickoff (today is 2026-07-13; this gives ~3 weeks of asset build. Slip to August 11 if the activation path (§10.5) isn't ready — do not launch without it.) Install / CTA (verified):npx mulmoclaude — the published one-command launcher. (npx create-mulmoclaude does not exist; never ship it.)

## 0. Positioning — the assistant you grow; harvest first, seed second (read this first)

The vision in one paragraph (from the vision doc): everyone imagines an AI assistant that knows everything about them and supports their work and life around the clock. That assistant is not for sale anywhere. The device (glasses, phone, watch) is only a doorway; the model (GPT, Claude) is only the engine. What makes an assistant valuable is how much it knows about you — your conversations, calendar, contacts, notes, and the apps you use. Every major AI company knows this, which is why they are all racing to accumulate your memory — and that is exactly why something this important should not be entrusted to one company. The only assistant worth having is one you grow yourself, on your own machine. MulmoClaude is the field (畑): empty at install, cultivated by conversation.

On every 3-second surface — headline, hero-video cold open, tweet #1 — prove the claim "you can't buy this" by SHOWING a grown assistant doing something no fresh chatbot could, then reveal how cheap the seed was:

A three-week-old assistant answers "what did I spend on client dinners this quarter, and which restaurant should I book for Friday?" — composing across an invoice tracker and a restaurant list it built itself when its owner asked, weeks apart, in plain conversation. Smash-cut back to Day 1: an empty folder, one sentence — "build me an invoice tracker" — and the app appears.

That is the hook, and it has two beats in a fixed order: harvest → seed. The harvest (a personal assistant that visibly knows you) is the thing money can't buy — it earns the stop-scroll. The seed (you got there just by asking; no code, no setup per app) is what makes it feel attainable — it earns the try. Reversing the order ("look, it builds apps!") re-enters the crowded app-builder category we are deliberately leaving. On any moving surface (hero video, 15s loop), land both beats inside the first 15 seconds. Never open with abstractions ("memory architecture," "schema," "DSL," "harness," "local-first") — show a grown assistant; the theory comes after.

The one thing at the center: the assistant, and the fact that you grow it. Everything else radiates from that:

- It grows by conversation. Ask for an app — a restaurant list, an invoice tracker, a vocabulary trainer — and it appears, no code, no plugin, no awareness of code at all. (Programmers call letting AI write code "vibe coding"; here you don't even see the code.) Each app is a small, one-person tool that was economically unthinkable to build before AI drove software cost to ~zero.
- Everything it learns stays. Conversations become a cross-linked wiki; structured data lives in the apps it built; nothing evaporates between sessions. A week in, it answers from your accumulated context. A month in, it composes across it.
- It's with you everywhere. Log in with the same ID from your phone and your PC and you reach the same assistant — the relay server only forwards messages and stores no data or apps. Later: glasses, headsets. The assistant's home is your machine; the devices are doorways.
- It works while you sleep. Scheduled sources, morning briefings, due-date nudges — the field keeps growing between visits.
- It cannot be taken from you. Plain Markdown/JSON in one local folder, git-friendly, open source (MIT). The anti-lock-in argument is not feature #4 anymore — it is the founding rationale, stated early and plainly.

The honest tension this framing creates (name it, don't hide it): PH rewards instant gratification; nurturing pays off over weeks. An "empty field at install" is the truth and the anti-demo. Resolution, in order: (1) the demo shows the grown state, time-lapsed — never the empty field alone; (2) the activation path (§10.5) is a tour of a mature, 30-day-old assistant, not a blank install; (3) onboarding promises a "first seed in 5 minutes" — one ask, one app, one thing remembered — so Day 1 has its own payoff.

Audience tension #2 — consumer vision, dev channels. The vision speaks to everyone ("no programming knowledge needed"), but day-one voters are Claude power users and self-hosters. Resolution: the anti-lock-in half of the vision is native to engineers — "every AI company is racing to own your memory; yours should live on your disk" lands harder on HN/r/selfhosted than any feature. To engineers, frame it as: "self-host the memory layer every AI company wants to rent you — and let the agent grow its own tools inside it." The consumer surface stays warm ("grow your own"); the dev surface leads with sovereignty. Phase-2 audiences (productivity, knowledge workers, enterprise) arrive later. JP is no longer phase-2 — the vision doc is a Japanese narration script and Satoshi's JP audience is strong; JP gets its own first-class beat (§8).

2026 reality check: app generation, rich output, mobile AI, sandboxing are commoditized — never lead with any of them. Even "ask → app appears" is now table stakes as a demo (Lovable/Bolt/V0 do a version of it); what they cannot say is "and three weeks later it's part of an assistant that knows you." Always attach the growth clause.

## 1. Taglines & category

### Product Hunt listing fields

- Name / headline (≤60) — FINAL:MulmoClaude — The assistant you can't buy. Grow yours. (55 chars)
- Tagline (≤60) — FINAL:It learns you, builds your apps, and lives on your machine. (59 chars)

Pairing logic: the headline states the vision's thesis as a provocation — "you can't buy it" stops the scroll (every reader assumes AI assistants are exactly the thing you CAN buy), and "grow yours" is the resolution and the invitation in two words. The tagline then makes "grow" concrete in three verbs: learns you (memory), builds your apps (extend by asking), lives on your machine (ownership / anti-lock-in). The arc is provocation → resolution → the three concrete things it means.

Why the headline leads with the negation. "Personal AI assistant" is the most crowded phrase of 2026 — Siri, Alexa, Copilot, Meta AI all claim it, and a viewer who sees only "AI assistant" scrolls. The negation "you can't buy" is simultaneously true (no vendor sells an assistant pre-loaded with your life), differentiating (it disqualifies every incumbent in four words), and an argument (it implies the memory-race critique without stating it). "Grow yours" then names the only path — which happens to be our product.

Headline — locked for the listing. Alternates kept only for social A/B (the PH name is one field):

Headline | Note 
---|---
Chosen | The assistant you can't buy. Grow yours. | Provocation + resolution; the vision's ¶1 in eight words 
alt | Grow an AI assistant that's actually yours | Warmer; loses the stop-scroll negation 
alt | Your AI assistant should live on your machine | Sovereignty-first; best for HN/r/selfhosted, colder on PH 
alt | Ask for an app. It becomes memory. | v1 headline — the app-gen control; kept for A/B only 

Tagline — locked. Alternates for social A/B:

Tagline | Note 
---|---
Chosen | It learns you, builds your apps, and lives on your machine. | Three verbs = the three pillars, concrete 
alt | Memory, apps, and data that grow with every conversation. | Growth-forward; softer on ownership 
alt | An open-source field where your AI assistant grows. | The 畑 metaphor, literal; may read twee in English 
alt | Every AI company wants to own your memory. Keep it. | The sovereignty knife; use on X/HN, not PH 

### The positioning bet — "the assistant you grow," not "AI app builder" and not "AI assistant"

Both adjacent categories are knife fights: "AI app builder" (Lovable, Bolt, V0, Replit) and "AI assistant" (Siri, Alexa, Copilot, ChatGPT). The uncontested ground is the conjunction the vision identifies: an assistant whose value comes from accumulated personal context, grown by its owner, on hardware its owner controls. No incumbent can follow — their business model is the accumulation happening on their servers.

The value of an AI assistant is not the model's IQ — models are rented engines, the same for everyone. The value is how much it knows about you, and that is precisely the asset you should never build inside someone else's walled garden. Growing it at home is the product.

How to deploy it:

- PH / consumer surfaces: warm phrasing — grow, nurture, yours, it knows you. The critique of the memory race appears once, in the maker post, as motivation — not as a crusade.
- HN / dev / self-hosted surfaces: lead with soverei

cross_cutting.content:
# Rackspace signs capacity agreements with Together AI and Blacksmith

Deployment planned for 2027

Rackspace has signed two customer agreements for compute capacity.

The first agreement is with neocloud startup Together AI and is a multi-year AI infrastructure agreement under which Rackspace will provide and operate dedicated Nvidia GB300 NVL72 infrastructure for Together AI.

Deployment is planned for 2027. Rackspace will also operate the associated power, liquid cooling, networking, and storage.

“Enterprise AI requires more than access to compute. Success depends on bringing compute into production, operating it reliably and delivering sustained value. That requires deep infrastructure and engineering expertise combined with operational accountability,” said Gajen Kandiah, CEO of Rackspace. “Rackspace brings more than 25 years of experience operating complex enterprise environments. Today’s announcement provides an opportunity to apply that experience to the dedicated infrastructure supporting Together AI’s inference platform.”

The companies also entered into a separate, non-binding letter of intent (LOI) to explore a joint go-to-market approach for enterprise-focused AI solutions, with Together AI providing inference capabilities and Rackspace providing the supporting AI infrastructure.

"Scaling in the enterprise requires infrastructure that can grow with our ambitions while delivering the performance and reliability customers expect," added Vipul Ved Prakash, founder and CEO of Together AI. "Rackspace brings the infrastructure engineering and operational expertise to support that growth, and we look forward to exploring additional opportunities together."

How much capacity Rackspace is providing to Together AI has not been shared, nor has the data center it will be deployed in, beyond that it is a "purpose-built, liquid-cooled facility, supported by Nvidia networking."

The second contract is with Blacksmith, an infrastructure platform for building and testing code.

Another multi-year agreement, Rackspace will provide Blacksmith with dedicated compute powered by AMD Epyc CPUs along with storage, totaling approximately 2MW of capacity located in Northern Virginia. Rackspace operates a data center in Ashburn, Virginia. Deployment will begin in early 2027.

“When we talk to developers and engineering teams, we keep hearing that AI is making it much easier to write code, but getting those changes tested and ready to ship is becoming the bottleneck. We’re building Blacksmith to help developers merge code faster and feel confident about what they’re shipping. Our partnership with Rackspace will help us scale the infrastructure behind that work,” said Aditya “JP” Jayaprakash, co-founder and CEO of Blacksmith.

Rackspace has an existing agreement with AMD to deploy 30MW of dedicated AMD compute across its data centers through 2028.

In addition to the customer contracts, this month Rackspace entered into a share purchase agreement with an investor group led by Voss Capital, LP, providing for an aggregate $66 million private placement of Rackspace common stock.

The company will use the funding for general corporate purposes, working capital, capital expenditures, and growth capital, including funding for GPU-related initiatives. Rackspace said it expects to seek separate financing for the purchase of the Nvidia GB300 NVL72 systems for Together AI and is in active discussions with potential lenders; however, no definitive GPU financing commitment has been obtained as of the time of writing.

cross_cutting.description: Teradata, Dell and NEXTDC sign sovereign AI MoU in Malaysia The three companies will offer an integrated sovereign AI stack at NEXTDC’s KL1 data centre, with Teradata targeting banks and the public sector first. Teradata, Dell Technologies and NEXTDC have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to set up a joint sovereign AI environment for Malaysian enterprises at NEXTDC’s KL1 data centre in Petaling Jaya.
cross_cutting.content:
# Teradata, Dell and NEXTDC sign sovereign AI MoU in Malaysia

The three companies will offer an integrated sovereign AI stack at NEXTDC’s KL1 data centre, with Teradata targeting banks and the public sector first.

Teradata, Dell Technologies and NEXTDC have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to set up a joint sovereign AI environment for Malaysian enterprises at NEXTDC’s KL1 data centre in Petaling Jaya.

Under the MoU, signed on 4 November, Dell’s GPU servers and storage and Teradata’s data and agentic AI software will be housed at KL1 as a single integrated stack. NEXTDC is supplying a facility built for high-density, GPU-intensive workloads, while Teradata’s software layer handles data management and governance, along with agentic AI tools that run directly on enterprise data.

The companies said the aim is to help Malaysian enterprises move AI projects from proof of concept into production, naming financial services, telecommunications, government and manufacturing as target sectors.

Josh Abbott, Teradata’s vice president for Asia Pacific and Japan, described the agreement in a media Q&A after the signing as “a commitment to sovereign AI.”

## Sovereign AI stack runs on Dell hardware

Abbott said customers would buy all their hardware through Dell, which partners with Nvidia for GPUs, with the cost passing through to the customer.

“In the Teradata Factory stack, it’ll be all Dell hardware and it’ll be in partnership with Nvidia,” he said.

Teradata Factory, which Teradata unveiled in May, packages its software with Dell compute and storage for on-premises deployment.

Abbott said compliance with US export rules on GPUs would also rest with Dell, which runs much of its Asia Pacific and Japan manufacturing in Malaysia; Teradata has not manufactured its own hardware since 2012. He said he had not run into any problems on that front so far, adding that it was still early days for this business in Malaysia.

No KL1 capacity has been set aside for the collaboration yet. “We don’t have anything predetermined right now in that regard,” Abbott said.

## Banks lead the pipeline

Teradata’s initial targets are financial services and the public sector, which Abbott attributed to their regulatory requirements and low tolerance for error. He could not name any customers.

“Right now in our pipeline, the banks are where we’ve got the most traction,” he said.

Sumash Singh, Dell Technologies’ managing director for South Asia and Emerging Markets, said in his address at the MoU signing that enterprises’ main challenge now was making sure AI delivered tangible business benefits, with access to the technology no longer the main hurdle. He cited Dell research showing that poorly integrated infrastructure still holds companies back from deploying AI more widely.

Luke Mackinnon, NEXTDC’s senior vice president and managing director for Asia, said in his address that KL1, which opened in May, is being built in phases towards 65MW of total capacity by 2028. The facility holds Uptime Institute Tier IV certification for its design and construction, and operational certification is still in progress.

cross_cutting.title: SoftBank and Grab plan US$1.85bn seed capital for AI infrastructure in Malaysia
cross_cutting.description: SoftBank and Grab plan US$1.85bn seed capital for AI infrastructure in Malaysia The two companies and Sarawak’s PETROS plan to build AI infrastructure across Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia ... SoftBank Group and Grab Holdings have signed joint development agreements to build AI infrastructure in Malaysia, with plans for US$1.85 ... Sarawak Berhad (PETROS).
cross_cutting.content:
# SoftBank and Grab plan US$1.85bn seed capital for AI infrastructure in Malaysia

The two companies and Sarawak’s PETROS plan to build AI infrastructure across Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, targeting five gigawatts or more of compute capacity, with funding released in stages against development and customer contract milestones.

SoftBank Group and Grab Holdings have signed joint development agreements to build AI infrastructure in Malaysia, with plans for US$1.85 billion in initial combined seed capital alongside Petroleum Sarawak Berhad (PETROS).

SoftBank’s proposed share is US$1 billion, with US$750 million from Grab and US$100 million from PETROS, the companies said on 9 November. The money will be deployed in stages, subject to the projects meeting development and customer contract milestones and the necessary closing conditions.

The long-term goal is at least five gigawatts of AI compute capacity across Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia under a multi-year plan. The partners will look for more investors and hyperscaler customers to support development and expansion. They expect the facilities, once fully operational, to rank among the largest AI infrastructure facilities of their kind in Asia, serving governments and businesses that need access to advanced computing.

## Two projects, two lead shareholders

The Sarawak project will be developed jointly by all three parties and builds on a framework agreement signed in Kuching on 8 October. Its proposed initial investment is US$1 billion, with US$800 million from SoftBank and US$100 million each from Grab and PETROS. Grab has an option to increase its stake, which would reduce SoftBank’s share, although SoftBank would remain the majority shareholder.

The Peninsular Malaysia project has US$850 million in proposed seed capital, with US$650 million from Grab and US$200 million from SoftBank. As founding shareholder, Grab will lead its development and bring in long-term strategic investors as it scales. Further development is expected to be funded at the project level through third-party equity and non-recourse project financing.

Grab co-founder, chairman and CEO Anthony Tan is expected to oversee both projects and appoint dedicated management teams to run day-to-day operations, while continuing to lead Grab. Grab’s board has reviewed and approved his affiliation with the projects. SoftBank has also agreed in principle to a five-year lock-up on Grab shares held directly by an entity within SoftBank Group, subject to customary exceptions.

## Demand for AI infrastructure in Malaysia and the region

Citing the e-Conomy SEA 2026 report by Google, Temasek and Bain & Company, Grab found that per capita AI usage across Southeast Asia’s six largest economies is around a tenth of the US level, and it projects that regional usage could grow up to 60-fold by 2030.

SoftBank chairman and CEO Masayoshi Son linked the investment to Malaysia’s potential role in that growth. “AI infrastructure will power the next wave of growth, and Malaysia has the talent and ambition to help lead it,” he said.

Tan said the infrastructure would help Grab speed up its work on localised AI for the region. “Together with SoftBank Group, we plan to build critical AI infrastructure in Malaysia, where Grab began, for all of Southeast Asia. This infrastructure will allow us to accelerate the development of localized AI solutions for our communities,” he said.

The projects will be developed in collaboration with the Federal Government and the Sarawak Government. They are aligned with the National AI Action Plan 2026–2030 (AI Nation 2030) and Sarawak’s Post COVID-19 Development Strategy 2030. The companies said the facilities will follow Malaysia’s renewable energy use guidelines and use high-efficiency designs intended to cut water use and reliance on local power grids.

The partners will also explore advanced manufacturing in Malaysia.

cross_cutting.content:
Intel Forms AI Alliance With 23 Korean Companies

스크롤 이동 상태바

# Intel Forms AI Alliance With 23 Korean Companies

## K-AI Full Stack Alliance launched at Intel AI Summit Seoul 2026 to target sovereign AI with Korean-made servers

Intel is joining forces with 23 South Korean companies to build AI infrastructure tailored to the Korean market.

The company has launched an alliance spanning hardware, software and AI services, centered on domestically manufactured servers powered by Intel chips. Together with Korean partners, Intel aims to target the sovereign AI and physical AI markets.

Tae-Won Bae, president of Intel Korea, announced the launch at the Intel AI Summit Seoul 2026, held at COEX in Seoul on Nov. 11. “Today marks the official launch of the K-AI Full Stack Alliance,” Bae said. “It represents our commitment to creating innovation together with Korean companies on an open infrastructure and ecosystem built around domestically manufactured servers.” He added that Intel would work closely with local partners and the government to support the development of Korea’s AI ecosystem.

The K-AI Full Stack Alliance is a broad coalition of domestic AI companies centered on Intel. It was established to build a comprehensive AI ecosystem in Korea, covering the entire technology stack. The alliance held its launch ceremony at the event, with 23 initial participants, including KTNF, Dnotitia, Panmnesia, Upstage, Nota AI, DEEPX, FuriosaAI and Exina.

Alliance members will collaborate across the AI industry, including hardware, software, industry-specific AI solutions and services. The partnership aims to strengthen their ability to respond quickly and flexibly to the rapidly evolving AI market. Ultimately, the companies plan to build AI infrastructure using domestically designed servers, contributing to Korea’s sovereign AI capabilities.

Intel Korea will also sign a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Seoul AI Hub to strengthen the technological competitiveness and support the growth of domestic AI startups. The two organizations will help promising Korean AI startups enhance their development capabilities and expand opportunities for technical collaboration.

Other senior Intel executives also took the stage to share the company’s AI technology strategy and examples of innovation.

Santosh Viswanathan, Intel’s Asia-Pacific regional head, identified sovereign AI, personalized AI and edge AI as three areas where Korea could capitalize on emerging opportunities.

“Korea has numerous companies innovating in domestically developed large language models (LLMs), memory and infrastructure,” Viswanathan said. “Korea is particularly well positioned in personal and edge AI, which will create significant business opportunities for all of us.”

Dan Rodriguez, executive vice president and general manager of Intel’s Edge Computing Group, discussed how AI is expanding beyond PCs into edge computing and industrial environments. He also emphasized collaboration among hardware, software and ecosystem partners to deliver AI innovation in real-world settings.

“Intel is building an open AI ecosystem and a foundation of trusted partnerships while providing developers and partners with the tools they need,” Rodriguez said. “For example, Intel Core Ultra Series 3 is a system-on-chip (SoC) integrating multiple processing units, delivering seamless optimization and high performance per watt to meet the needs of edge customers.”

Anil Nanduri, head of AI product go-to-market at Intel’s Data Center AI Group, introduced the company’s server product lineup. Intel is mass-producing Clearwater Forest, a Xeon server processor featuring up to 288 high-density, energy-efficient E-cores. Next year, the company plans to launch Diamond Rapids, featuring up to 256 high-performance P-cores.

Intel also unveiled a physical chip from its next-generation data center inference accelerator lineup, the Intel GPU D-Series. The high-efficiency accelerator delivers up to 26,200 TFLOPS of FP4 performance while consuming 350 watts of power. Compared with the competing Nvidia RTX 6000 Pro, Intel demonstrated advantages including 30% lower latency on Gemma models, 2.2 times higher AI agent performance and up to 5.9 times higher computing performance in financial simulations.

cross_cutting.content:
# SC26: Fermaca Unveils Nvidia-Powered AI Factory Platform to Power Mexico and Latin America

## Mexico's first Nvidia Cloud Partner brings its energy and infrastructure capabilities together with Nvidia accelerated computing to build a new base for AI production in the region
This is a Press Release edited by StorageNewsletter.com on November 12, 2026 at 2:00 pm 
Fermaca announced its designation as the first Nvidia Cloud Partner (NCP) based in Mexico, the first of its kind in the region and unveiled an AI factory platform designed to position the country as a producer of advanced AI capabilities for Mexico and Latin America.Beginning with Fermaca Digital Origins in Mexico City, the phased rollout combines Fermaca’s infrastructure development and operating experience with the Nvidia accelerated computing platform to expand access to the computing capacity businesses and institutions need to build and deploy AI.

Fermaca’s strategy reaches across the physical infrastructure behind AI, from gas molecule to token. It brings the group’s capabilities in gas infrastructure and energy development together with fiber connectivity, AI facilities and accelerated computing. This integrated approach is intended to address the infrastructure constraints that determine where AI can be built and how far it can scale, creating a foundation for Mexico to serve growing demand across the region.

These developments are designed to advance Mexico’s economic progress and strengthen its digital sovereignty by building the capacity to develop and deploy AI on infrastructure located in Mexico. Coupled with local expertise, this capacity can help Mexican businesses, universities and institutions address national priorities and retain more of the knowledge and economic value created by AI.

“Fermaca is investing in Mexico’s capacity to produce intelligence, create economic value and shape its own technological future,” said Manuel Calvillo, project coordinator infraestructura, Fermaca. “Our ambition runs from gas molecule to token: connecting the energy and digital infrastructure needed to produce intelligence at scale. With Nvidia accelerated computing, we are extending the infrastructure we know how to build into the computing capacity on which businesses across Mexico and Latin America will increasingly depend. Our purpose is to make these developments a lasting contribution to Mexico’s progress and the prosperity and wellbeing of its communities.”

“We’re excited to support Mexico’s growing AI ecosystem and bring Nvidia accelerated computing to more businesses and developers,” said Marcio Aguiar, director, enterprise, Latin America Nvidia. “As an Nvidia Cloud Partner, Fermaca is building an AI factory powered by Nvidia B300 NVL72 systems to help enterprises across Mexico and Latin America develop and deploy AI using their own data.”

A new foundation for AI adoption across the region
Fermaca’s platform is designed to connect regional customers with Nvidia AI infrastructure in Mexico. Enterprises can use that computing capacity to develop models around their own data and bring AI into their operations, while developers and research institutions gain a foundation for new applications. For Nvidia and its ecosystem, the rollout creates a new route to serve Mexican and Latin American demand as local AI adoption grows.

Fermaca Digital Origins is the first deployment in the platform, with an initial Nvidia Blackwell Ultra cluster. A subsequent deployment roadmap incorporates Nvidia Vera Rubin. Inventec is providing compute systems and DDN is providing storage, with Fermaca responsible for infrastructure development and operations.

“Fermaca is connecting the infrastructure that powers industry with the infrastructure that will power intelligence,” said Paul Bloch, chairman and cofounder, DDN. “Its vision creates a significant opportunity for Mexico to become a producer of AI at scale and serve customers across Latin America. DDN is proud to support that ambition with the data infrastructure designed to keep Nvidia GPUs supplied with data and turn advanced computing into productive AI capacity.”

“Today marks the beginning of a long-term partnership between Inventec and Fermaca. We are excited to combine our engineering expertise and Nvidia-powered compute systems with Fermaca’s infrastructure capabilities, and we are committed to growing together as Fermaca expands its AI platform across Mexico and Latin Americ,” Inventec Corporation.

Fermaca’s near-term plan targets 60 MW of total facility power supporting operational AI facilities by December 31, 2027, including computing, cooling and supporting facility systems. Beyond that milestone, Fermaca Digital City in Durango represents a longer-term ambition of up to 1 GW of IT capacity, which measures computing equipment only. These are separate development milestones, with deployment phased as the platform expands.

Fermaca has received the full support of Mexican government authorities at the federal, state and municipal levels, reflecting a shared commitment to building the infrastructure for Mexico’s AI economy. This coordinated support strengthens Fermaca’s ambition to position Mexico as a strategic hub for AI production and services across Latin America and advance the national development objectives of Plan México.

Consistent with its longstanding commitment to the communities where it operates, Fermaca approaches development across the full value chain: from gas and energy infrastructure to engineering, digital connectivity, AI computing and education. The aim is to turn investment into lasting local opportunities, strengthen skills and contribute to Mexico’s shared prosperity and the wellbeing of its people.

Working with Nvidia, Fermaca continues to develop “México Aprende IA con Fermaca y Nvidia” whih started in Durango, an education initiative designed to equip university teachers with AI knowledge, teaching resources and practical training they can bring into their classrooms. By preparing educators to reach successive generations of students, the program aims to build local talent and enable more Mexicans to participate in the opportunities created by AI.
